articles.title: Jayden Daniels Gets The Better Of Joe Burrow: 3 Takeaways From The Commanders' Win
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels delivered some impressive heroics to beat Joe Burrow and the Bengals. Here are Steven Ruiz's takeaways.
articles.body: A rainstorm and a temporary blackout couldn’t stop the Bengals and Commanders from giving us an electric Monday night affair for the second time in three seasons. History repeated itself as Jayden Daniels led a game-winning drive to seal the upset, just as he did back in September 2024 in Cincinnati. Daniels and the offense got off to a slow start in the driving rain, but the third-year quarterback eventually found his rhythm, guiding six consecutive scoring drives to end the game. That was enough to overcome some shaky decision-making by Dan Quinn. The Bengals will feel like they let this one slip away. Joe Burrow was his efficient self for most of the night but made a few uncharacteristic mistakes late. Still, the defense had a chance to close it out, but just couldn’t get a stop down the stretch. Here are my takeaways: 1.Jayden Daniels Overcame Dan Quinn's Conservative Decision This may have been the most impressive game of Daniels’ career, which says a lot for a quarterback who produced one of the best rookie seasons in NFL history. It didn’t look that way earlier, with Daniels struggling to cope with the rain. He was inaccurate and skittish in the pocket, taking a handful of early sacks. But the two-minute drill before the half seemed to unlock something in the Commanders star. It was this dart to tight end Chig Okonkwo that really opened the floodgates for Washington’s passing game. Daniels hasn’t been great at targeting the middle of the field early in his career, but that wasn’t the case on Monday night. He made several strong throws that attacked the middle of the Bengals defense, including two lightning bolts on the game-winning drive. This one to rookie Antonio Williams set up Drew Stevens for an easy chip-shot winner. It felt like Daniels had to win the game twice thanks to his coach. Washington faced a fourth-and-very-short at the Bengals' 24-yard line with 2:30 remaining. Next Gen Stats’ fourth-down decision model had it as a clear "go" situation, and that’s without accounting for the quarterback on the other sideline. Stevens nailed the kick, but it took only two plays for Burrow to get the Bengals in range for the go-ahead kick. If not for Daniels’ heroics, Quinn would’ve faced some tough questions in his postgame presser – something he’s gotten comfortable doing this season. 2.Joe Burrow Lost Ground In The MVP Race Based on the traditional box score, Burrow put up another high-quality performance against Washington. He threw for 324 yards on 29-of-38 passing and also tossed a pair of touchdowns. But, really, the MVP candidate got away with a number of ill-advised throws that should have been intercepted, including one on Cincinnati’s final drive that would have ended the game. Burrow followed that up with a brutal sack that nearly knocked the Bengals out of field goal range. Fortunately, kicker Evan McPherson bailed him out with a 56-yard field goal that would have been good from 65. We can’t be too harsh on Burrow for making a few mistakes. The Bengals are asking him to carry the offense to make up for the non-existent run game. With that increased usage rate, he’s bound to mess up eventually. And Burrow had enough bright sorts to consider this a good performance. His pocket presence and accuracy were on full display throughout the night. Washington couldn’t capitalize on Burrow’s turnover-worthy plays, but MVP voters were watching. And after seeing Brock Purdy’s near-perfect outing against the NFL’s best defense on Sunday night, there has to be a changing of the guard at the top of the MVP ladder. 3.The Bengals Don't Have A Run Game To call the Bengals' running game bad would be an understatement. It was straight-up useless on Monday night, gaining just 31 yards on 14 carries with a success rate of just 7%. After the rain let up, Cincinnati immediately abandoned it and turned the game over to Burrow and the passing game. It’s difficult to pinpoint any one issue. The run blocking has been just fine, the design is unimaginative, and the running backs can’t create anything on their own. It would be interesting to see how it would perform with more star power in the backfield. The numbers suggest Chase Brown and Samaje Perine are leaving a lot of meat on the bone. Brown was particularly ineffective on Monday night, mustering just six yards on six carries against a below-average Commanders run defense. The early struggles in the passing game may have been a harbinger of things to come if the Bengals do run into bad weather come playoff time. Asking Burrow to drop back 50 times in bad weather against playoff-caliber defense may not be a winning business model. The quarterbacks they could face, like Josh Allen or Patrick Mahomes, are pretty good, too. You have to wonder if the Bengals will look back at the trade deadline with regret. Some good running backs may have been available for the right price, including Jonathan Taylor. Sure, Cincinnati would’ve had to part ways with valuable draft capital, but Super Bowl windows don’t stay open for long. This could be the franchise’s best shot at winning its first title. It will be harder to get through January without a run game. 3 ½. What's Next? The Bengals suffered a setback in their quest for the AFC’s No. 1 seed, but they do have one of the easier schedules in the league, so this may not be the blow it feels like in the moment. Cincinnati will take on the Saints and the Browns over the next two weeks and can’t afford to drop another game, with Mahomes and the Chiefs visiting Paycor Stadium in Week 14. That looks like a must-win game for Cincinnati to stay in the race for home-field advantage. The Commanders kept their playoff hopes alive and could be in a decent spot if they take care of business the next two weeks. They get the Cardinals and Titans next. Win those games and get some help from the Giants' opponents, and Washington could be in first place by mid-December thanks to the tie-breaker over New York. The postseason is still very much in play.

articles.title: 7 Plan B Trade Options for NHL Teams That Missed Out on Dylan Larkin
articles.summary: Dylan Larkin is a Montréal Canadien, and teams that missed out must now look elsewhere.
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin is a Montréal Canadien, and teams that missed out must now look elsewhere.

Now that he and Connor Hellebuyck are both on new teams, we're left wondering about what's next. For teams that wanted Larkin, their attention turns elsewhere to find a veteran goal scorer.

For the teams that didn't land the 30-year-old center, finding another player to fill that need may not be quite as difficult as trying to pull someone with a limited trade list. Then again, some of the players who could be their next targets may also have trade protection to navigate.

There are plenty of teams who could use a lift, and not quite as many players out there who could be had. Let's take a look at who is and could be out there soon.

If the Penguins are going to be open for business, a lot of attention will be paid to their biggest-name veterans to see if they'll be willing to go elsewhere for a shot at another Stanley Cup.

Buzz has been circling around Sidney Crosby, but it's Evgeni Malkin we're keeping our eyes on.

Crosby departing the Penguins would be a shock, and it's not something we're anticipating happening, but Malkin has always had an air of mystery around him despite playing his entire career in Pittsburgh as well.

Malkin has long been mentioned in trade rumors, and the public pressure on the Penguins to bring him back this season was notable. That makes us think that if any of the Penguins' "Big Three"—Crosby, Malkin, and Kris Letang—is moved, it will be Malkin.

That's not to ignore Erik Karlsson, of course, who is also in the final year of his contract, but we've resigned ourselves to believing he'll be playing somewhere new before the trade deadline in March anyway.

If Malkin goes, though, it will be fascinating to see which contender steps up to add one of the game's greatest players of the past 20 years.

Elias Pettersson has been in trade rumors for a few years now, and even though he's got an $11.6 million cap hit through 2032, he's having a bit of a bounce-back season this year and has a history of being a high-end scorer when things in Vancouver haven't been bordering on disaster.

Pettersson's skill and hockey smarts make him a top player in the league, and there's no doubt that part of what goes through any interested general manager's mind is how well he would perform away from a team that has struggled as much as the Canucks have the past few seasons.

Even though Larkin was traded with an $8.7 million cap hit through 2031, Pettersson's juicy contract would still be a difficult one to move, and that's before considering he has a full no-move clause.

As much as Pettersson loves Vancouver, you wonder if its recent run of tough play, coupled with interest from a contender, might be enough for him to waive it.

One of the players who went to Detroit in the Dylan Larkin trade to Montréal was Kirby Dach. He's due to be a free agent in July, and if the Red Wings are looking to secure more futures, trading the newly acquired big forward might be in their plans.

Given that Michael Hage was the big pickup for the Red Wings in the Larkin deal, retaining Dach likely only comes with a contract extension, and with how tricky this season has already been for Dach, he might welcome that.

Then again, with where the Wings are organizationally after trading the former team captain, Dach may be open to going elsewhere, especially if it's a contender calling for him. After all, he got a good taste of the postseason last year with the Canadiens, and that is looking like a long shot with Detroit. With eight points in 22 games this season with the Habs, we'll be curious how he performs with the Red Wings and if he can remain healthy to take advantage of his new opportunity.

It seems that for the past few seasons, Ryan O'Reilly's name comes up when teams are looking for a veteran center who's a proven winner. The 2019 Stanley Cup champion and Conn Smythe Trophy winner is an obvious mark for trade talk, but with the Nashville Predators competing for a playoff spot and playing well so far this season, you wonder if that will still be the case.

O'Reilly is an obvious target for trade talk not just because of his proven history, but also because he's in the final year of his contract, which has a $4.5 million cap hit , and doesn't have any kind of trade protection. It's somewhat of a surprise he wasn't traded last season while the Predators struggled, but there's something to be said for appreciating a veteran player who'd rather stay where he is than pack up and move regularly.

At 35 years old, teams know what they're going to get from O'Reilly, and that he's still an effective player only makes him more desirable to other teams. But so long as the Predators are in the playoff race, it's hard to see them moving him.

With the Pittsburgh Penguins struggling terribly to start the season, GM Kyle Dubas may have a lot of work on his hands this season to change things up. One player who could be had is forward Rickard Rakell.

Rakell has another year beyond this one left on his contract with an affordable $5 million cap hit. With a history of goal scoring and solid two-way play, he would be an attractive player for other teams to acquire and one the Penguins would ideally be able to get a solid return on.

Rakell has three 30-goal seasons and three other seasons with at least 20 goals. This season, he's got 13 points in 23 games with eight goals.

There's no doubt a contending team would love to have a player like Rakell, but he's got no-trade protection, per PuckPedia.com . His eight-team no-trade list could hinder the ability to trade him.

The Calgary Flames are down bad this season and very well could be (should be?) sellers this season. One player who could be had is forward Morgan Frost.

The 27-year-old forward is in the final year of his contract with Calgary, and his $4.375 million cap hit is more than affordable for any team. He had his best goal-scoring season a year ago with 22 goals, and historically he's good for around 40-50 points per season. As far as middle-lineup forwards go, he'd make a great depth addition for a contender.

Frost has done well with the Flames over the past couple of seasons, but if a team wants to add him, they'll need to not be on his eight-team no-trade list. With how tough it's been in Calgary, you'd have to think Frost would be OK with a change, particularly when heading into a new contract.

The Bruins are off to a great start this season, but even teams in good positions can still make a big deal with a player in a contract season, and the B's have a couple of them in Pavel Zacha and Casey Mittelstadt. It's Zacha who we're keeping our eyes on closely for a trade, however, because his two-way ability and how he's developed his offensive game in recent years make him an attractive player.

The Bruins have been aggressive with re-signing their own players (Fraser Minten, Morgan Geekie) as well as adding big-money players in trades (JJ Peterka), and with Zacha in the final year of his four-year deal with a $4.75 million cap hit and coming off a 30-goal season a year ago, that price is going up. Although the salary cap ceiling is also going up, with Zacha at 29 years old, you wonder if Boston would be eager to add another long-term, big-money extension to go with the others they've already got done.

Zacha is a valuable player, and his work on their second line with Mittelstadt and Peterka has been good, with 17 points in 22 games. But with the money they've spent on Minten, the hope they've got in Matthew Poitras, and the growth of James Hagens, you wonder if there's a move to be made here with Zacha to get something back for a player they may not be looking to extend.

articles.title: NHL Trade Update: How will Austin Roest and James Stefan benefit from their moves between Edmonton Oilers and Nashville Predators
articles.summary: Explore the recent NHL trade involving Austin Roest and James Stefan as the Edmonton Oilers and Nashville Predators swap young forwards to enhance their development pipelines.
articles.body: The Edmonton Oilers and Nashville Predators have agreed to a minor trade that involves forwards Austin Roest and James Stefan, exchanging the two in a one-for-one deal. Meanwhile, Nashville has traded Roest to Edmonton, with Stefan going the other way as both franchises adjust their organizational depth.The deal won’t have an immediate impact on either NHL roster, but it allows both players to continue their development in different surroundings. For the Oilers and Predators, the deal is a relatively low-risk move that could help their respective development systems.Austin Roest and James Stefan headline NHL tradeThe Nashville Predators have traded Austin Roest to the Edmonton Oilers for James Stefan, a one-for-one forward swap, the teams announced Friday. The deal brings another young forward into Edmonton’s development pipeline and gives Nashville Stefan as it reorganizes its organizational depth.Austin Roest is a right-shot forward, 22 years old, who was originally selected by the Nashville Predators in the sixth round (175th overall) of the 2023 NHL Draft. The forward is 5-foot-10, 185 pounds, and has experience playing in the ECHL, AHL, and WHL.This season, 2026-27, Roest has played 15 games for the Atlanta Gladiators, Nashville’s ECHL affiliate. He has three goals and four assists for seven points during that stretch.He also appeared in 41 games with the Milwaukee Admirals during the 2025-26 season in the pro ranks. Roest had a goal and seven assists for eight points and 10 penalty minutes.Prior to turning pro, Roest established himself as a productive forward playing with the Everett Silvertips in the Western Hockey League. In 210 junior games, he scored 89 goals and 107 assists for a total of 196 points.After the deal, Roest is expected to join the Bakersfield Condors, the Edmonton Oilers’ AHL affiliate. It will allow him to continue his development and compete for a bigger role within the forward group of the organization.His junior production shows he can produce offensively, but it’s a big step to be able to do that on a consistent basis in the professional game. A change in organization might present a new chance for building confidence and more consistency.Why did Nashville Predators acquire James Stefan?James Stefan gives the Nashville Predators another forward option within the organization's development structure. The one-for-one swap suggests Nashville sees some upside in bringing Stefan into its system and moving on from Roest.We don’t have the trade details to know Stefan’s stats, contract status, or what he’ll be asked to do right away. His potential role will become clearer as the organization makes decisions.It’s the type of move that ultimately reflects the minor roster moves NHL teams make when managing the development of prospects. This deal isn’t adding an established NHL regular to either organization, but it is allowing young forwards to take their next professional steps.Roest hopes to capitalize on the chance in Bakersfield with the Edmonton Oilers. Meanwhile, the Nashville Predators will take a look at what Stefan can bring to their depth at forward. articles.title: "I was killing myself"- 14-time WWE Champion Charlotte Flair recalls the struggles of saving her previous marriages
articles.summary: Charlotte Flair has emerged as one of the biggest female WWE superstars of all time.
articles.body: Charlotte Flair has emerged as one of the biggest female WWE superstars of all time. The 14-time WWE Women’s Champion has carved out an illustrious and highly successful career; however, the same cannot be said when it comes to her personal life. Flair had three unsuccessful marriages in the past, and she recently opened up about the struggles of saving each of them.Charlotte Flair says she was trying hard to save her marriagesIn a recent interview with Insight with Chris Van Vliet, Charlotte Flair was asked about still wanting to have a family and children amid her WWE career. Flair admitted that while she did want it, she was not ready to settle for it. This led The Queen to say that she did the same in her previous marriages, especially in her last one with former WWE star Andrade. Flair even went on to reveal that she was ‘killing herself’ to make her marriages work.Charlotte Flair said, “Unfortunately, I’ve settled three times, and in my last one, like, it broke my heart. And it wasn’t over obsession for my job. And it also was not over—it was things out of my control. And part of what I was killing myself was trying to be perfect in my marriage for things not to happen, and perfect here.”Charlotte Flair’s third marriage ended in 2025Charlotte Flair and Andrade began dating in 2019 and tied the knot in 2022. However, their marriage lasted only two years, and their divorce was finalized in October 2025. Post-that, Andrade left WWE to rejoin AEW, while Flair is still a part of the active roster and has been a part of the tag team division with Alexa Bliss.What is next for WWE megastar Charlotte Flair?Charlotte Flair is next set to be a part of the 2026 edition of WWE Survivor Series PLE. The Queen will team up with Alexa Bliss, Stephanie Vaquer, Tatum Paxley, and Bayley against Fatal Influence (Jacy Jayne, Lainey Reed, and Fallon Henley), Jade Cargill, and Michin in the Women’s War Games match. articles.title: “Go baby !!!”: Leon Draisaitl's wife Celeste Desjardins celebrates Edmonton Oilers superstar's latest NHL career achievement
articles.summary: Celeste Desjardins expresses her joy on Instagram as Leon Draisaitl, Edmonton Oilers superstar, hits 1,100 career NHL points during a game against the St. Louis Blues.
articles.body: Leon Draisaitl's wife, Celeste Desjardins, shared her excitement after the Edmonton Oilers forward reached 1,100 career NHL points. Her two-word reaction, “Go baby !!!,” appeared on Instagram Stories following the Oilers' social media celebration of his achievement.Draisaitl accomplished the feat in Edmonton’s game against the St. Louis Blues on Sunday, Nov. 22. The German center added another memorable performance to his resume, continuing his impressive scoring surge and establishing himself among the NHL’s most prolific scorers.Leon Draisaitl reaches 1,100 NHL points for Edmonton OilersCeleste Desjardins celebrated Leon Draisaitl's 1,100-point achievement with an enthusiastic Instagram Stories message, showing her support for the Edmonton Oilers superstar.Desjardins commented on an Instagram post of the Oilers celebrating: “Go baby!!!”Her brief response hinted at how much the milestone meant to her personally, and offered a glimpse of the support system behind Draisaitl’s professional success.The reaction also brought back her previous celebration when Draisaitl hit 1,000 career NHL points in December 2025. That time, Desjardins wrote a longer tribute, calling her husband amazing and saying how proud she was of him.Her latest message was considerably shorter but carried the same supportive sentiment. As Draisaitl continues to achieve major career milestones, Desjardins has remained an encouraging presence away from the ice.How Leon Draisaitl reached the 1,100-point milestoneDraisaitl recorded his 1,100th NHL point during the second period against the St. Louis Blues. The goal came 9:15 into the period following a give-and-go sequence with teammate Vasily Podkolzin. Draisaitl moved past the St. Louis defense before sending a shot beyond goaltender Joel Hofer.The goal gave the Edmonton Oilers a 2-0 advantage at Enterprise Center and marked Draisaitl's 23rd goal of the season. At that stage of the campaign, he also led the NHL in goals scored.According to the milestone statistics reported after the game, Draisaitl became the ninth player in Edmonton Oilers history and the 72nd player in NHL history to record 1,100 regular-season points. He achieved the accomplishment in 881 games, with 457 goals and 643 assists.Celeste Desjardins has an established acting careerWhile Leon Draisaitl has built his reputation through professional hockey, Celeste Desjardins has developed her own career in the entertainment industry.She is an actress from Sudbury, Ont., who has appeared in several film and television productions. She has credits in the 2017 TV series Taken, where she played the role of Cali Mills, and the Lifetime thriller productions of Obsession, where she played Madison Turner.She has also appeared in Hallmark projects, including An Ice Palace Romance as Lori Mitchell and Fashionably in Love as Avery Gilligan. Her earlier work includes appearances in the Flower Shop Mystery movies and the Canadian comedy series Letterkenny.Desjardins also shares a close connection with another prominent Edmonton hockey family. She is a longtime friend of Lauren Kyle McDavid, wife of Oilers captain Connor McDavid. Their friendship helped bring the two couples closer, eventually creating a connection within the team's wider social circle.Draisaitl and Desjardins made their relationship public in 2018 through photographs from a vacation in Greece. Their relationship continued for several years before the Edmonton Oilers forward proposed during a trip to Mallorca on July 11, 2024.The couple married on August 2, 2025, at Château d'Estoublon in Provence, France. Several members of the Edmonton Oilers organization were reportedly present for the celebration.Their relationship has since attracted attention from hockey followers, particularly when Desjardins publicly celebrates her husband's achievements.The last “Go baby !!!” message adds another personal element to Draisaitl’s professional journey. With the Edmonton Oilers forward still chasing big career milestones, his 1,100-point milestone is another big chapter in his NHL legacy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor Bedard Undergoes Surgery, Latest on Blackhawks Star's Shoulder Injury and Timeline to Return
articles.summary: Chicago Blackhawks announced Connor Bedard underwent successful shoulder surgery on Monday and the expectation is that the captain will "make a full recovery in an approximate timeline of four months," according to ESPN.com.
articles.body:
Chicago Blackhawks announced Connor Bedard underwent successful shoulder surgery on Monday and the expectation is that the captain will "make a full recovery in an approximate timeline of four months," according to ESPN.com .

The Blackhawks placed Bedard on injured reserve on Sunday, retroactive to Nov. 17.

Bedard suffered the right shoulder injury during Chicago's 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday.

The 21-year-old has dealt with health woes as of late, previously missing 12 games due to a right shoulder injury during the 2025-26 season.

Although he didn't need surgery at the time, he eventually underwent a procedure on his left shoulder due to an injury that occurred while he was training over the offseason.

Bedard was forced to miss Chicago's first six games this season as he recovered.

He eventually returned to appear in 15 contests, recording seven goals and 11 assists.

Bedard has been a key contributor for the Blackhawks throughout his career, as the 2024 Calder Memorial Trophy winner is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he amassed a career-high 75 points despite being limited to 69 games played.

His latest absence is a tough blow to a Chicago squad that has only compiled a 8-14-2 record to start this season.

Mendoza's first start came in one of the toughest possible matchups against the Seahawks in Week 10. Unsurprisingly, he struggled in that contest, but there were signs of fantasy upside, including his six carries for 22 yards and a touchdown.

This week, we got a better idea of what Mendoza could become for fantasy and the results were excellent. Even with Brock Bowers out of the lineup, Mendoza threw for 267 yards and three scores versus the Broncos, adding another 22 yards on the ground. That locks him in as a top-five fantasy QB on the week.

The Browns aren't the most fantasy-friendly opponent and the Raiders have a bye in Week 14, but over the final month (including the fantasy playoffs) Mendoza has one of the five best schedules at his position with dates against the Chargers, Broncos, Titans and Cardinals. He's firmly in the high-end fantasy QB2 mix with low-end QB1 potential given his late season slate.

Watson is also someone worth considering as a fantasy starter this week and beyond.

The Browns have one of the softest schedules the rest of the way, including the Raiders, Bengals, Falcons, Giants, Ravens and Colts. That stretch begins with a Raiders defense that's top-five in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

Cleveland hasn't had many favorable opponents for Watson, but he finished as a top-10 weekly fantasy QB in the two games against easier defenses (Titans in Week 5, Texans in Week 10).

You can expect that to happen at least a few more times given his rushing stats and the Browns' strong, young pass-catching corps of Denzel Boston, KC Conception and Harold Fannin Jr.

If you need a real-life example of what Black could do if CMC were ever sidelined, just look at what happened with Emmett Johnson when Kenneth Walker III sat out the last two weeks. Don't let players with that kind of upside remain on the waiver wire.

Bhayshul Tuten is one of the breakout stars of the 2026 season, but he's missed or been limited in several practices over the last few weeks. To his credit, the sophomore back has managed to suit up every week. Unfortunately, he missed time on Sunday while battling the injuries, leading to just a 43% snap share and 13 touches for 53 scoreless yards in the loss.

If the Jaguars are serious about contending for a Super Bowl, they need their star runner healthy for the stretch run, which makes you wonder if they will ever give him a week off. This week's matchup with the Titans seems like the perfect opportunity to get Tuten some rest, since Jacksonville is 14.5-point favorites.

In that scenario, Rodriguez would step into the lead role and be a potential fantasy RB1 given the opponents and likely positive game script.

Sampson hasn't had the biggest stat lines since returning from injured reserve, but he has been productive with yardage totals 77, 69, 48 and 37 over the last four outings.

More importantly, he out-snapped Quinshon Judkins in three straight outings, turning this backfield into a 50-50 committee.

Without a Judkins injury, the ceiling is limited with Sampson, so keep your expectations in check. But he's definitely worth considering as an RB3/flex option.

Even without Lamar Jackson, Hill has been productive over the last three games. The veteran pass-catcher has at least eight touches in each of those outings, while amassing 92 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 9, 38 yards and five receptions in Week 10, as well as a season-high 98 yards and a TD on Sunday.

Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after the loss to the Panthers, so he should be fine for Week 12 barring any symptoms popping up over the next 24 hours. However, even with Henry starting, we've still seen Hill have a set role in the offense, with the duo splitting snaps fairly evenly over this three-game span.

Jacoby Brissett has given Hill 12 targets during his two starts and that doesn't seem to be going away. Fantasy managers can target Hill as an RB3/flex with some upside thanks to his pass-catching and occasional big plays.

Saquon Barkley appeared to injure his shoulder and potentially suffered his second stinger of the season on Sunday. After the game, Barkley admitted he won't be 100% for the rest of the season, but remained confident he would play Thursday against the Cowboys.

If Barkley is right, then Shipley would only be a flex option thanks to a good matchup with the Cowboys. However, if Barkley ends up being held out on Thanksgiving, Shipley would become one of the top pickups of the week.

Knight hasn't made a huge dent in the box score over the last two games, but it's worth remembering that the Cardinals squared off against two tougher run defenses in the Rams and Chiefs.

The reason I'm mentioning Knight now, is due to the Cardinals' remaining schedule. The Commanders and Eagles are on deck the next two games, followed by a bye in Week 14. Then things get more interesting with the Jets, Saints and Raiders during the fantasy playoffs. Each of those defenses ranks inside the top-10 for most fantasy points allowed to running backs.

If Jeremiyah Love isn't activated from IR, Knight has a chance to produce as a sneaky fantasy option in those matchups.

Kenny Gainwell is 54% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add behind Black and Rodriguez, if available.

Williams had his best outing of the season on Monday night, totalling nine receptions and 122 yards on a team high 11 targets.

The rookie has now posted at least 50 yards or a touchdown in four of his fives games since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season. However, this most recent performance shows a new ceiling in a Commanders' passing attack that has a very favorable schedule in the coming weeks. Washington will take on the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons over the next month.

First-year players often improve in the second half of the season as they get more comfortable in the offense and earn the trust of teammates and coaches. Williams is on that exact script at the moment and should be considered a fantasy WR3 with upside the rest of the way.

It's not a great week for fantasy receivers on the waiver wire, which is why Douglas is leading this section despite only managing 30 yards against the Bills.

The rookie has posted at least 70 yards in four of his seven appearances this season. That includes some very strong volume in the last three weeks, with at least eight targets in each of those outings.

It's hard to trust anyone catching passes from Kyle McCord, but Douglas remains in the WR3/flex mix. However, just like Kaelon Black, I'm going to exclude him from the top-10 pickups since I've highlighted him enough in past weeks.

Hurst's five catches, 56 yards and two touchdowns on seven targets was one of the more shocking outcomes from Week 11. I was high on the rookie prior to the season, but his playing time had dwindled down to just 2% of the snaps in Week 9 and he hadn't caught a pass in any of his last three outings.

Coming out of the bye, the Buccaneers clearly made an effort to emphasize him and his snap share rose to 64% — his highest mark since Week 3.

After the contest, Todd Bowles told reporters the team plans to feature Hurst more moving forward, especially early in games. With Emeka Egbuka disappointing and Chris Godwin Jr. fading, it only makes sense to see what they have in Hurst. This performance puts him in the WR4/flex conversation as a boom-or-bust option.

With Wan'Dale Robinson out for the season, Dike becomes a very intriguing fantasy add in an uptempo Titans' offense that's come to life over the last month.

In the first game with Robinson on IR, Dike led the team in targets (seven) and played the second-most snaps among the receivers behind only Carnell Tate. The result was six receptions and 69 yards with another four yards on the ground. It's his second solid stat line over the last three outings, after he posted a 5-71-1 day in Week 8.

While it might feel odd to invest in the Titans' passing attack, this is a team that's finding its identity as the season progresses. Dike can excel as a playmaker in this environment. He also has a decent schedule coming up with the Jags, Commanders, Lions, Colts and Raiders over the next five weeks.

Mumpfield hasn't taken advantage of the opportunity he's been given this season with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams missing so much time.

Now that Nacua and Terrance Ferguson are done for the season and Adams isn't expected back until mid-December, there is another chance for the 24-year-old wideout to step up. Based on where I have him placed in this column, you can probably tell I'm skeptical. Mumpfield has been held to 20 yards or less and really only popped up for bigger days twice thanks to big plays in those games.

I expect the Rams to lean on their defense, rushing attack and tight ends to grind out wins until Adams returns in a few weeks. But if you're in a deeper format and searching for help at receiver, Mumpfield has a path to production.

Jakobi Meyers is 52% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Douglas, if available.

Tre Tucker is 53% rostered but would be the No. 4 WR add behind Douglas, Meyers and Williams, if available.

Michael Pittman Jr. vs. DEN (24% rostered)

Xavier Hutchinson vs. BAL (29% rostered)

Harrison Wallace III vs. WAS (0% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

It's tough sledding at tight end this week, but as I mentioned in the Konata Mumpfield section, Puka Nacua and Terrance Ferguson are out for the year and Davante Adams isn't expected back for another couple weeks at the earliest.

Higbee hasn't produced much in the way of yardage over the last month, but he did have that strong three-game stretch earlier this year with stat lines of 8-62-1, 5-67-0 and 5-83-0. He also caught a touchdown in their last game before the bye. The Rams are running out of bodies and Higbee is one of the few healthy players who has a proven history with Matthew Stafford. If you need help immediately though, Higbee might not be the best option since the Packers are a tough matchup this week. If you're specifically looking for a Week 12 streamer, you can always consider the usual options below.

Streaming options (if healthy and starter is out)

Risky streaming options (if healthy and starter is out)

Darnell Washington vs. DEN (5% rostered)

Quarterbacks: Drake Maye, Lamar Jackson, Aaron Rodgers

Running Backs: Tyler Allgeier, J.K. Dobbins, TreVeyon Henderson

Wide Receivers: Puka Nacua, A.J. Brown, Chris Godwin Jr., Marvin Harrison Jr.

Tight Ends: Juwan Johnson, Hunter Henry, Jake Ferguson

Not a lot of surprising names on the drop list this week, but it's time for fantasy managers to do some house-cleaning since most of these players are rostered in over 50% of leagues.

Nacua is out for the season and it's unlikely we'll see Maye or Jackson again. Don't waste your time holding out hope for those star quarterbacks to return in the final week or two.

Johnson's production had declined and now he's dealing with a hamstring injury, so feel free to use that roster spot for someone with more upside.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 12 Panic Meter: Emeka Egbuka isn't in a slump anymore — this is who he is
articles.summary: The Chiefs backfield, Trey McBride, Colts offense and more from Ray Garvin in the Week 12 fantasy football panic meter.
articles.body:
We're past the point in the fantasy football season where we can afford to be patient. It's playoff crunch time, and for a lot of fantasy managers, every lineup decision over the next few weeks could be the difference between making the postseason and watching from the sideline.

There's no time to sit around waiting for players to figure it out. We need production, and we need it now.

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

I know the noise around Kenneth Walker III is loud right now. Rookie Emmett Johnson has been sensational in the games Walker has missed, and fantasy managers are wondering if we're witnessing a changing of the guard in Kansas City.

The word out of Kansas City on Monday, via Eric Bieniemy, is that Walker remains the starter when he's available. When K9 is on the field, K9 is the lead ball-carrier in this offense.

That "when he's available" part matters, though. Walker was listed as a non-participant on Monday's estimated practice report with a groin injury. Keep an eye on his status heading into Week 12 on Thursday night against the Bills.

Here's what I will say: Johnson has earned a meaningful role in this offense. Think of him as a souped-up, "Super Saiyan" version of Jerick McKinnon. He deserves to be on the field, and his involvement shouldn't disappear when Walker returns. I can absolutely see Johnson settling into an 8-to-12-touch-per-game role, which could take something off Walker's ceiling.

But the way this Chiefs offense is humming right now, both on the ground and through the air, there's room for both backs to be productive. When Walker gets healthy, this has a chance to be one of the best backfields in the NFL, if not THE best.

If Walker is healthy and active, he's in your lineup. Don't let Johnson's emergence talk you out of starting K9. Also, don't let Walker being active deter you from flexing Johnson.

Panic level: No Panic (for me)/Total Panic (if you're still a believer)

Emeka Egbuka has now gone 16 consecutive appearances without reaching 65 receiving yards, dating back to last season. He's seen five targets in each of his last two games, totaling 56 receiving yards. Meanwhile, rookie Ted Hurst III just found the end zone twice for Tampa Bay.

This is a far cry from the receiver who lit up the first half of his rookie season.

So why am I not panicking? Because I've already adjusted my expectations. Egbuka isn't a WR1 or even a high-end WR2 at this point. He's a WR3 with the potential to deliver WR2 or WR1 production in any given week. If that's how you're valuing him, nothing from Week 11 should shock you.

No panic doesn't mean he's a must-start. He's a WR3 or flex option, and there are going to be weeks when you have better options on your roster.

Now, if you're still holding onto the version of Egbuka we saw during the first half of his rookie year, you should be in total panic territory.

Sixteen appearances isn't a slump anymore. That's who he's been.

Panic level: Some Panic (bordering on Total)

Trey McBride probably belongs in total panic territory, but the sheer volume of opportunities he's getting makes it difficult to put him there.

The Cardinals are down to their fourth-string quarterback in journeyman Josh Johnson. There was legitimate concern about what that would look like against Kansas City on Sunday, but McBride still managed to draw a season-high 14 targets, turning them into nine receptions for 54 yards.

Fourteen targets for 54 yards. That's where the concern lies.

There isn't much happening downfield for McBride in this version of the Arizona offense. It's to get the ball in his hands as quickly as possible and hope he can make something happen after the catch. Touchdown opportunities are going to be difficult to come by, and the Cardinals still haven't settled on who will start at quarterback moving forward.

The volume is enough to keep McBride in your lineup, but expecting him to provide the type of positional advantage we've become accustomed to is probably unrealistic right now.

Close to total panic? Absolutely. Am I recommending that you bench Trey McBride in a 1-TE league? No.

It wouldn't be a Panic Meter without a New York Jets player, and unfortunately, we have to talk about Garrett Wilson once again.

At the start of the year, I thought this would be the season Wilson finally got north of 15 half-PPR points per game. Instead, we're looking at another season in that 13-14-point-per-game range.

This isn't a talent issue. We may have seen the best version of the Jets offense on Sunday, and that's exactly the problem for Wilson's fantasy outlook.

Breece Hall and Braelon Allen combined for 36 carries and 161 rushing yards. Geno Smith was incredibly efficient when asked to throw the football, completing 17-of-21 passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Wilson played 90% of the offensive snaps and was still the team's leading receiver.

Wilson's involvement isn't the issue. There just aren't enough passing opportunities when the Jets are leaning on what I consider one of the best 1-2 punches at running back in the NFL.

If the Jets can run the football effectively, limit what they're asking Geno to do and capitalize on his passing opportunities, why would they change that?

He's still an every-week fantasy starter for most managers, but he's a WR2 with upside rather than the high-end WR1 many of us hoped he would become this season.

Indianapolis Colts offense (Jonathan Taylor, Tyler Warren)

After sleepwalking through much of the season, the Indianapolis Colts finally did what a lot of fantasy managers wanted to do weeks ago. They'd had enough of Daniel Jones, released him and handed the keys to Anthony Richardson Sr.

Does that make this offense better? Probably not.

Richardson hasn't proven that he's the answer to the Colts' passing game, and he's stepping into an offense that's already without two important pieces.

No Josh Downs. No Quenton Nelson. No Daniel Jones. No problem, right?

Where things could improve is in the running game. Richardson's ability to keep the football on read-option plays gives opposing defenses something else to account for and could open up rushing lanes for Jonathan Taylor. Of course, that same rushing ability could also cost Taylor carries and touchdown opportunities around the goal line.

Taylor and Tyler Warren aren't necessarily in the same situation, though.

Taylor's workload had been declining as rookie Seth McGowan earned more opportunities. McGowan's hamstring injury could push some of that volume back in Taylor's direction, although we don't have a clear timeline for McGowan's return.

JT has been borderline unplayable lately and continues to slide down my weekly rankings. There is at least a realistic path for him to get back on track if the volume returns and Richardson's presence helps the rushing attack.

It's much more difficult to see that path for Warren. In four games since returning from injury, Warren has caught 11 of 25 targets for 85 yards.

Maybe Richardson has been sitting on the bench all this time thinking, "When I get my opportunity, I've got to get the ball to Tyler Warren."

That's blind hope, faith and optimism at this point.

Warren is going to be outside my top-15 tight ends for Week 12. If there's a dependable option on your bench or somebody available on the waiver wire, make that move.

A quarterback change doesn't automatically fix a bad offense. Taylor has a path back to fantasy relevance through volume, but neither player deserves automatic consideration in your starting lineup right now.

Welcome to the Coping Corner, Indianapolis.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares who can help your lineup in Week 12
articles.summary: These depth running backs could prove to be useful to fantasy football managers in Week 12.
articles.body:
Let's take a look at the backup RBs who have a Yahoo roster rate under 60% and could help fantasy football teams to victory this week. Players are ranked in order of their Week 12 appeal, and their current roster rates are listed in parentheses.

The Bucs had to vacate their preferred run-heavy game plan when they fell behind to the Lions in Week 11. But Gainwell continued to find ways to contribute, gaining 57 total yards on four carries and four catches.

Bucky Irving continues to be the unquestioned RB1 in this offense. But the Bucs WRs have disappointed this season , which has opened an opportunity for Gainwell to be more involved in the passing attack. He would normally rank a bit lower on this list but is a viable flex option for a matchup against a Panthers defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

Hill is starting to turn heads as a viable weapon in Baltimore's offense. The 29-year-old was as dangerous as any Ravens skill player in Week 11, when he tallied 69 yards and a touchdown on six carries while also gaining 27 yards on four catches. Hill has caught at least three passes in each of his past six games and has amassed at least 69 rushing yards in three of his past seven contests. He could be a viable flex option no matter what the game script looks like for the Ravens. After all, while franchise QB Lamar Jackson was likely to tuck the ball and run, new starter Jacoby Brissett is more likely to dump it off. Hill is heading into a matchup against an average Texans defense.

Johnson is sitting on waivers in most leagues, as many managers have forgotten that he produced 110 rushing yards and a touchdown in the Packers' two games before their Week 11 bye. With Josh Jacobs expected to miss another game with a broken finger, Johnson should lead the team in carries against the Rams on Wednesday night. There are two things preventing Johnson from ranking at the top of this list – he has no involvement in the passing game, and the Rams have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

Perine outperformed Chase Brown on Monday Night Football, gaining 97 total yards on six carries and four catches, in comparison to 36 total yards on six carries and five catches. Although Brown has received a little more than double the carries of Perine this season, both backs are averaging 3.8 yards per carry, while Perine has averaged nearly twice as many yards per catch. After a strong effort in Week 11, Perine could be used more than normal in Week 12, when the Bengals host a Saints defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

Knight did his part to keep the Cardinals offense afloat in a difficult Week 11 road game with Josh Johnson at QB by gaining 35 yards on seven carries and catching his only target for a 10-yard gain. The injury-riddled Cardinals desperately need a more reasonable matchup, which they will get in a home game against the Commanders. While the fantasy upside of any member of Arizona's offense remains limited by the QB situation, Knight is the favorite to lead Arizona in touches for that game.

Although Rodriguez wasn't called upon often in the Jags' loss to the Giants in Week 11, he produced 41 total yards on four catches and one catch. The former Commander would normally rank lower on this list, but he and the rest of Jacksonville's offense have tremendous potential for their home matchup against the Titans.

Since trading Jeffery Simmons on Oct. 29, the Titans have allowed an average of 45 points over three games. Rodriguez should get more touches than usual if the Jags jump out to a big lead. It's also worth noting that Bhayshul Tuten was banged up during the Week 11 loss. If the Jaguars opt to rest Tuten for a game in which they are two-touchdown favorites, Rodriguez would jump to the very top of this list.

In four games since returning from a season-opening stint on injured reserve, Sampson has had a clear role as the Browns' pass-catching back. The second-year pro has averaged five carries and four catches per game, and with 4.2 yards per carry and 9.5 yards per catch, he is making the most of his opportunities. Sampson should be able to approach 10 points in PPR formats during against a Raiders defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to RBs.

After gaining at least 50 yards on the ground in three consecutive games, Black had a dismal night (six carries, eight yards) in the 49ers' lopsided win over a stout Vikings defense. One bad game isn't enough to knock the rookie off this list, as he still ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards and has earned at least six carries in each of his past seven games. While Black remains on the radar for flex consideration, it's worth noting that he is heading into another tough matchup when the Niners host the Seahawks.

The bad news for Washington is that Week 11 served as a redemption game for Ashton Jeanty, who averaged 7.2 yards on 11 carries while continuing to be a weapon as a receiver out of the backfield. Fortunately, Washington had a solid game of his own, averaging 4.7 yards on nine carries. Washington will remain low on this list each week due to his lack of involvement in the passing game, but he still gets 6-10 carries in almost every game.

The good news is that Kamara has scored three times in the past two weeks. The bad news is that he has gained just 16 total yards in those two contests. The Saints clearly trust Kamara in the red zone, which gives him some potential in deep leagues. And perhaps he will get more opportunities overall when the Saints face the Bengals in a possible shootout.

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 12 but are an injury away from having significant value.

articles.title: African rivals fret over Morocco’s growing football dominance
articles.summary: As Morocco enjoys success on and off the pitch, is it benefitting from preferential treatment, or setting an example?
articles.body:
Morocco’s growing influence in African football is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

From reaching the semifinals of the 2022 FIFA World Cup to hosting major continental competitions and preparing to cohost the 2030 World Cup , it has arguably become Africa’s dominant footballing nation.

Morocco is also preparing to welcome FIFA’s 77th Congress in Rabat on March 18, 2027, and the country hosted the last two editions of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Awards. Three of its players – Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari – feature on the 10-person shortlist for the 2026 men’s CAF Player of the Year award.

For some, Morocco represents what sustained investment, strategic planning and football diplomacy can achieve. Others, however, question whether its growing concentration of hosting opportunities and institutional influence is creating an imbalance within African football.

Kamilla Swart, an associate professor and Director of the Master of Science in Sport and Entertainment Management programme at Hamad Bin Khalifa University in Doha, Qatar, says Morocco’s current position is the product of a strategy developed over several years.

“I think it’s a case of Morocco building its expertise over a long period of time,” she said.

“So if you even think of, you know, everybody talks about the Mohammed VI Football Academy that was inaugurated in 2010. So it’s not something that’s just happened now.”

Morocco bid unsuccessfully to host the World Cup several times before finally winning a joint bid for 2030. Swart said those bids enabled the country to assess its weaknesses and establish the infrastructure needed to compete for major international events.

However, Swart said that Morocco’s repeated hosting of CAF events has raised questions about whether other African countries are getting sufficient hosting opportunities.

“On the one hand, I can understand why all these events are going to Morocco,” Swart said.

“And on the other hand, I can see the point of view where there may be some scepticism or mixed feelings about that – potentially the rest of the continent is not benefitting from that.”

Some have also accused CAF of giving Morocco preferential treatment. These concerns intensified following the controversial 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final between Senegal and Morocco. Senegal initially won the game 1-0 after extra time, but the match was overshadowed by a late penalty awarded to Morocco, prompting Senegal’s players to temporarily leave the pitch in protest.

On March 17, 2026, CAF’s Appeal Board overturned an earlier disciplinary ruling, declared Senegal to have forfeited the final by leaving the pitch under Articles 82 and 84 of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) regulations and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of an appeal by Senegal and reinstated them as champions on Tuesday.

Speaking before that ruling, Kenyan sport lawyer and arbitrator Khayran Noor told Al Jazeera, “I think we need to distinguish between two issues: Morocco’s genuine institutional and infrastructural progress, and the responsibility of CAF to ensure that its decision-making processes are transparent and beyond reasonable suspicion.”

When it comes to awarding hosting rights, a CAF Executive Committee assesses the facilities and documentation submitted by bidding countries before making the final hosting decision.

However, Noor believes the process would benefit from greater transparency, including published evaluation criteria, independent technical assessments, disclosure of potential conflicts of interest and explanations of final decisions.

She also warned against allowing financial strength to translate into disproportionate political influence. Article 17 of the CAF Statutes provides each member association with one vote at the General Assembly, irrespective of its financial capacity.

“Morocco should be entitled to benefit from its investments, but every other African federation should have a meaningful opportunity to demonstrate its own capacity,” Noor said.

“Ultimately, institutional confidence is built not only by making the right decisions, but also by demonstrating that those decisions were reached fairly.”

Morocco’s hosting profile also has an important commercial dimension, some experts say. CAF depends heavily on broadcasting and sponsorship revenues, making the quality of its competitions and broadcasting standards central to its financial sustainability.

Gerard Akindes, a Beninese-born sports management scholar, international consultant and former professional athlete, believes the concentration of major competitions in Morocco is partly down to the uneven quality of football infrastructure and broadcasting production elsewhere on the continent.

“AFCON is what makes CAF’s revenue,” Akindes told Al Jazeera. “And they want the best product possible that they can sell to broadcasters to generate revenue that is going to sustain the organisation.”

Akindes also suggested that Morocco’s willingness to host competitions when other countries were unable or unwilling to do so had strengthened its relationship with CAF.

“Morocco managed to get a lot of influence because they saved the organisation several times by hosting events that nobody wanted to host,” he said. “When you do that, they probably get some return.”

Morocco’s growing presence on the CAF Awards shortlist has also generated debate over preferential treatment.

The 2026 ceremony returns to Lagos on December 2, marking Nigeria’s first time hosting the event since 2014. However, the absence of Nigerian players from the men’s Player of the Year shortlist has attracted criticism, particularly among supporters who expected players such as Victor Osimhen, Ademola Lookman and Calvin Bassey to feature.

Morocco, meanwhile, has three nominees, including reigning winner Hakimi.

CAF-accredited journalist and Brila Media contributor Adeniyi Adebanjo believes the reaction should be considered alongside the performances of the shortlisted players and the wider dissatisfaction among African football supporters following the controversy surrounding the 2025 AFCON final, particularly CAF’s handling of the disciplinary proceedings and their decision to award Morocco a 3-0 victory.

He rejected suggestions that the rescheduling of the awards ceremony was connected to the dispute between Senegal and Morocco or intended to influence the voting process.

“I think this is a conspiracy theory,” he said. “I don’t necessarily ascribe to the idea that CAF is playing some type of game with this.”

Nigerian exercise physiologist and University of Lagos lecturer Victor Damilola Ademola – who has visited Morocco three times in the last 12 months – believes the country’s success reflects a systematic development of players at all levels of the game.

Morocco has also been effective in integrating eligible diaspora players into its national teams, strengthening its talent pool.

“They have invested significantly in training facilities, stadiums and sports science infrastructure, including facilities for youth development. The Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat is an excellent example,” he said.

“What matters is not just the facilities themselves, but how they support player development, conditioning, medical care and preparation across different age groups.”

Ademola cautioned against interpreting every Moroccan achievement as evidence of preferential treatment from CAF and argued that Morocco’s progress should also encourage other African countries to examine their own football administration, international engagement, infrastructure and player development.

“There is no established proof that CAF is deliberately favouring Morocco because of its investments or hosting contributions … [although] when similar concerns keep emerging, they deserve scrutiny rather than automatic dismissal,” he said.

“At the same time, we must not use these controversies to excuse our own shortcomings.”

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan says snooker players need more mental health support in wake of Mark Allen's struggles
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan has called for snooker players to be given more support for their mental health; O'Sullivan is competing in the Crucible Cup, a Snooker 900 tournament on Pluto TV; If you are affected by this story, please visit sky.com/viewersupport
articles.body:
The seven-time world champion's comments come in the wake of fellow professional Mark Allen's recent struggles, who told TNT Sports last month he was in a "bad place" during an emotional interview after a first-round defeat to Jordan Brown in the Northern Ireland Open.

Allen had spent 10 weeks in a mental health clinic before discharging himself to play in the competition and posted on X after the interview, saying he was "not OK" but wanted to show his "fighting qualities".

O'Sullivan has candidly reflected on his own struggles with depression and anxiety in the past, citing the intense pressure of professional snooker as a factor in driving him to the "worst time of [his] life" .

When asked if there was currently enough support in place for players on the tour, O'Sullivan told Sky Sports: "Probably not.

"I think if you ask any ex-professional you probably get 40 or 50 per cent of them going: 'yeah, I really struggled.'

The Essex native also referenced the isolating nature of snooker as a challenge for players, as opposed to team sports, where players are consistently supported by staff.

"In football, they have a lot of coaches, a lot of people to support them and do their food, just like golfers, who have a caddy to help them through.

"I think with snooker, you're just on your own and you're in your head. It's not like a sport where you get endorphins from running around for 90 minutes.

"Even if you get beat 7-0 [in a team sport], you could still feel all right, because the endorphins that you get from exercise are a happy drug.

"In snooker, you don't get that. So a lot of it's in your head - and I just think that for a lot of players, it would be good if they had that bit of support."

Allen thanks supporters after 'very tough' period

articles.title: Trick Calls Out The Rock & Cody Rhodes, WWE Rumors on Liv Morgan, Roxanne Perez & Paul Heyman
articles.summary: Bleacher Report brings you up to date on the latest news and rumors from the WWE universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report brings you up to date on the latest news and rumors from the WWE universe.

Trick Williams Sets Sights on The Rock, Cody Rhodes

Trick Williams' lemon pepper steppers have their next targets.

Just like everything the United States champion has done since his promotion to the main roster in January, Williams only wants to go big.

While speaking on Double Coverage Podcast (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Williams was asked to fantasy book one wrestler from any era to step into the ring with. He picked the man who made him want to become a pro wrestler in the first place.

"Of all time? I'm going, I'm going The Rock," said Williams. "Like, The Rock is the guy who made me really say, 'Okay, I'm going to wrestle now. I want to feel something like this.' Don't want to bite his swag. Not going to steal his catchphrase. It's just corny. You know what I mean?

"But like, man, the way he had control, the way he can make the people feel something. The aura, the swag, the way he represented culture. It was a culture movement, you know, just as much it was, you know, great for wrestling. And I always wanted something like that. Yeah. To me, I think The Rock is one of the greatest to ever do it."

The Rock is a timely pick after WWE announced he will return to programming during Saturday's Survivor Series event in Houston, Texas.

While there's no clear indication of his role on the premium live event, the company has celebrated 30 years since his debut on recent programming, so the expectation is likely to focus on some form of festivity.

We may not see The Anointed One vs. The Great One any time soon, but The Rock's emergence could tie into The Bloodline's ongoing feud with the 946, as the two factions prepare for War Games at the iconic event.

Williams is happy to throw options out there, though. Having beaten Sami Zayn for the first of his US title runs at WrestleMania 42 in April, he's got the name of another active great in mind for his first WM main event.

"I'm going to say Cody Rhodes," said Williams, per Double Coverage Podcast (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News). "I'm going to say Cody Rhodes. I mean, Cody is a guy, I mean, you just seen the ups and downs of his career. You see how he persevered and turned every situation into a home run. I have nothing but the most utmost respect for Cody Rhodes.

"So, you know, getting that opportunity to truly share the ring with him on such a high stage will be insane because he knows what it takes to make it to the top and to fight and scratch and claw. You know what I mean? Those are the type of guys you want to learn from and rub against and see if you got that 'It' factor."

Latest on Roxanne Perez Turning on Liv Morgan

A lot has happened since Liv Morgan's shoulder injury opened up a spot on The Judgment Day for Roxanne Perez back in June 2025.

Morgan has gone through extensive rehab, returned to win the Royal Rumble, and won the WWE Women's World Championship twice without the much-expected Roxy turn against her playing out.

Now embroiled in a feud with Becky Lynch, it's reported that Morgan won't need to worry about Perez flipping the script against her until we get into the build for Wrestlemania.

"It won't happen before WrestleMania," reported JoeyVotes of WrestleVotes (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News). "So don't expect it anytime soon, 'cause you're not gonna be able to pull it off if she does it, like, next week. Seeds will be planted, and we'll find out. For the split between Roxanne and Liv, you're going to do it for WrestleMania."

Such thinking has JoeyVotes claiming that The Prodigy may well follow in Morgan's footsteps and win the Royal Rumble.

"Which tells me she is the Royal Rumble winner, which I think will propel her character forward immensely," he noted. "She's still, what, 25 years old probably? And to have a Royal Rumble win, a WrestleMania title match against someone like Liv Morgan — you can make an entire career out of that, out of this next couple of months for Perez."

"She's in that position to do it. She has that win over Chelsea Green under her belt. It's like one of those, 'Hey, we wanna do this with you. It's not in the cards right now because of other circumstances, but we'll take care of you down the road.'"

Following such a path would certainly give Perez the springboard needed to dethrone Morgan, whose control over The Judgment Day centers around achieving things the other members can't.

If you listen carefully enough, the words 'BROCKKK LESNAAAAR' are still traveling down wind somewhere, such is the power of Paul Heyman, whose last appearance on WWE programming came back in October.

According to WrestleVotes' JoeyVotes (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), Heyman is likely to return soon, ready for the schedule to kick into gear as WWE enters Royal Rumble season.

"Paul Heyman is due to be back relatively soon," JoeyVotes reported. "Right now, you're in that kind of a holding period where you're getting around the bend here, getting to Survivor Series. This is when things play out as it pertains to not just Survivor Series, but leading into Royal Rumble and WrestleMania."

"All these things start to happen this time every year. So we'll have a guy like Paul Heyman back on TV."

WWE cooled Heyman's link to The Vision recently, after he appeared to side with Oba Femi rather than Bron Brekker during their feud to crown the future of the company.

Femi against The Vision continues to linger, with The Ruler calling for Heyman's group to stand down or face consequences on the latest episode of Monday Night Raw.

Femi turned down a potential alliance with Heyman after defeating Brock Lesnar once and for all at SummerSlam in August. It's highly likely we're heading towards a Femi vs. Roman Reigns programme that builds to WrestleMania 43 in April - two studs Heyman now has major storylines with.

articles.title: ¡Clasificada y con puntaje perfecto! Colombia derrotó 2-0 a Honduras y avanzó a 16avos del Mundial Sub-17
articles.standfirst: Colombia vence 2-0 a Honduras en el Mundial Sub-17: goles, resumen y clasificación a 16avos
articles.summary: Colombia vence 2-0 a Honduras en el Mundial Sub-17: goles, resumen y clasificación a 16avos
articles.body: La Selección Colombia Sub-17 derrotó 2-0 a Honduras este martes 24 de noviembre en el complejo Aspire Zone de Doha, Catar, por la segunda fecha del Grupo L del Mundial Sub-17 de 2026. Con este triunfo, el equipo dirigido por Fredy Hurtado alcanzó seis puntos de seis posibles —tras debutar con victoria 2-1 sobre Japón— y aseguró de manera anticipada su clasificación a los dieciseisavos de final. El partido no fue sencillo para la campeona sudamericana. Honduras planteó un bloque defensivo ordenado, exigió al límite la paciencia colombiana durante la primera mitad y probó con transiciones rápidas en el complemento, pero la expulsión de Diego Matute a los 53 minutos inclinó el escenario y los cambios desde el banquillo destrabaron el marcador en los últimos quince minutos. Durante los primeros 45 minutos, Colombia tuvo la posesión del balón pero encontró dificultades para romper el entramado defensivo de Honduras. El conjunto centroamericano resistió en su campo y apostó a cerrar los carriles interiores, obligando a la Tricolor a buscar alternativas por las bandas y en la pelota quieta. Las aproximaciones más peligrosas en ese tramo llegaron mediante remates y acciones de balón detenido: el arquero hondureño David Paz respondió con intervenciones clave —incluida una acción ante Adrián Mosquera y un intento acrobático de Jhan Moreno tras un tiro de esquina— para sostener el 0-0 al descanso. Del otro lado, Honduras intentó responder en velocidad y tuvo sustos en área colombiana, mientras el encuentro se mantenía tenso y disputado en la mitad de la cancha. El desarrollo del segundo tiempo cambió al minuto 53 cuando Diego Matute vio la tarjeta roja en Honduras, dejando a su selección con diez hombres. Sin embargo, la superioridad numérica no se tradujo de inmediato en tranquilidad para Colombia. Entre los minutos 66 y 72, la Tricolor atravesó pasajes de apremio ante un rival que no renunció al contragolpe. Mike Arana y Darwin Cruz generaron peligro por los costados, y Milton Moya tuvo una oportunidad clara tras un error en salida colombiana, pero se resbaló al definir y desperdició la ocasión. La lectura de Fredy Hurtado desde el banco resultó determinante para destrabar el duelo: Minuto 75 (0-1 · Matías Caicedo): Tras una jugada preparada en un tiro de esquina por el sector izquierdo, Samuel Martínez envió el centro y Matías Caicedo apareció libre en el segundo palo para empujar el balón y abrir el marcador. Minuto 83/84 (0-2 · José Escorcia): En el tramo final, un balón largo presionado por José Escorcia derivó en un error de control del guardameta David Paz; el atacante cartagenero recuperó la pelota de frente al arco y definió con comodidad para liquidar el partido.

articles.title: Anthem Singer Apologizes for Getting 'O Canada' Lyrics Wrong Before Maple Leafs vs. Islanders
articles.summary: The anthem performer who sang incorrect lyrics to the Canadian national anthem ahead of Monday night's matchup between the New York Islanders and Toronto Maple Leafs issued an emotional apology on social media.
articles.body:
The anthem performer who sang incorrect lyrics to the Canadian national anthem ahead of Monday night's matchup between the New York Islanders and Toronto Maple Leafs issued an emotional apology on social media.

Sarrah Strimel Bentley, a breast cancer survivor who sang at UBS Arena ahead of the Islanders' Hockey Fights Cancer night, said in a post on social media she was suffering memory-related issues related to cancer treatments.

"Getting up in front of 18,000 people and practicing an anthem that you haven't heard for your whole life is scary, and I botched the lyrics, and I'm really sorry," Strimel Bentley said.

"I got put in menopause because I had breast cancer, and tonight is about hockey fighting cancer, and menopause makes you forget things. So, I just wish that you'd be a little easier on someone who's just a human being."

The moment when Strimmel Bentley sang "we lend our hearts to thee" rather than "we stand on guard for thee" went viral after the broadcast seemingly showed Leafs captain Auston Matthews reacting to the error.

The Leafs then referenced incorrect lyrics in multiple social media posts shared during and after the 4-2 win.

The misremembered anthem might have ended up being good luck for the Leafs, who came away from the road game with their first win of November while snapping a nine-game losing streak.

articles.title: Cronología y reacciones del Real Madrid-PSV: la remontada que cambió la noche del Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El conjunto blanco pasó de sufrir a firmar una goleada espectacular
articles.summary: El conjunto blanco pasó de sufrir a firmar una goleada espectacular
articles.body: El Real Madrid vivió dos partidos en uno ante el PSV. Una primera parte para olvidar, con los neerlandeses castigando las carencias defensivas de los blancos, dio paso a una exhibición ofensiva tras el descanso. Valverde, Bellingham, Mbappé y Vinicius firmaron una remontada que dejó al Bernabéu con una sonrisa y a los tertulianos del Marcador de Radio MARCA con mucho que analizar. El PSV salió sin complejos y pronto encontró espacios en la defensa madridista. Ruben Van Bommel avisó en los primeros minutos y Vinicius respondió con un disparo al poste. Sin embargo, el equipo de Mourinho no logró imponer su juego y terminó pagando sus errores. Tchouaméni cometió un penalti sobre Mijnans que Perisic transformó en el 0-1. El gol dejó al Madrid tocado y al PSV con la posibilidad de ampliar su ventaja. Los neerlandeses llegaron con facilidad al área blanca y pusieron en evidencia las dudas de Militao y Rüdiger. Javier Tintó no tuvo reparos en definir la primera mitad: «La peor primera parte de la temporada, y la mejor segunda». Mourinho movió el banquillo en el descanso. Konaté, Huijsen y Bellingham entraron por Rüdiger, Militao y Tchouaméni. El Madrid ganó solidez atrás y encontró más espacios para atacar. La reacción fue inmediata. Valverde empató en el minuto 50 y, diez minutos después, Bellingham firmó un golazo desde fuera del área para completar la remontada. El inglés, que había comenzado en el banquillo, cambió el partido con su calidad y su presencia en el centro del campo. Mbappé amplió la ventaja en el minuto 64 y volvió a marcar en el 84, mientras Vinicius cerró la goleada en el 87. El Madrid pasó de sufrir a dominar y terminó el encuentro con un contundente 5-1. Javier Tintó destacó el impacto de los cambios y el momento de forma del inglés. «Por encima de todo está Bellingham, que es un jugador que ahora mismo no puede descansar, está en un momento espectacular. Hay que aprovecharlo, está de dulce», afirmó. Jaime Sánchez consideró que la falta de acierto del PSV permitió al Madrid llegar al descanso con opciones de remontada. «En la primera mitad estuvieron a merced del PSV, la poca eficacia de los holandeses dejó el marcador a solo un gol de diferencia», explicó. El exfutbolista también valoró la aportación de los centrales que entraron tras el descanso y la recuperación de Vinicius: «El hecho de que Vinicius vuelva a tener buenas sensaciones es bueno para el equipo, se necesita que vuelva a tener su tono». Pablo González Fuertes, analista arbitral de Radio MARCA, no quedó satisfecho con la actuación de Espen Eskas. «Espen no ha estado bien. Tuvo dos acciones en las que estuvo bien posicionado y no tomó decisiones», señaló. El especialista puso el foco en el penalti que adelantó al PSV y en la intervención del VAR, al considerar que la retransmisión televisiva ofreció la repetición de la jugada con mucha más rapidez. El Madrid se marcha del Bernabéu con una victoria que refuerza su confianza, pero con una exigente serie de partidos por delante. El Alavés, la Real Sociedad, el Atlético y el Arsenal serán las próximas pruebas para un equipo que no puede permitirse repetir la primera parte ante el PSV.

Fourteen teams will play seven Minnesota high school football state championship games Friday and Saturday at U.S. Bank Stadium. These are the players most likely to decide each Prep Bowl.

Class 1A: Springfield vs. Minneota, 10 a.m.

Parker Kuehn, QB, Springfield. Kuehn is a Mr. Football finalist and runs an offense that averages more than 50 points per game.

Tristen Sussner, QB, Minneota. Minneota brings a 58-game winning streak into the Prep Bowl. A fifth straight state championship would tie the state record. Sussner has 28 passing touchdown and eight rushing touchdowns this season.

Eli Rodemeyer, QB, Byron . Byron is in its first Prep Bowl and hasn't lost since Orono beat it 37-14 in September. Rodemeyer threw for four touchdowns and ran for six when the Bears beat Fergus Falls 42-41 in the semifinal.

Beau Nicklay and Jaymeson Smith, DEF, Byron. Both are Minnesota Duluth commits. Byron's best chance at an upset is these two slowing down the defending champs.

Finn Dyvik, QB, Orono. Orono is 12-0 and trying to win back-to-back titles. Dyvik has thrown for 1,854 yards and 22 touchdowns, and he's run for 958 yards and 15 touchdowns.

Class 2A: Jackson County Central vs. Caledonia, 4 p.m.

Jacob Kruger, QB, Jackson County Central . The sophomore had four total touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) in the semifinal win over Redwood Valley. JCC is going for its third straight Class 2A title.

Cooper Allen, LB, Caledonia. Allen leads the defense with 88 tackles. Caledonia has 11 state titles, but JCC has knocked it out of the state tournament twice in the last three years.

Class 6A: Minnetonka vs. Champlin Park, 7 p.m.

Miles Felton, QB/RB, Champlin Park . Felton is back from a broken wrist for the biggest game of the year. Champlin Park is the only unbeaten team in 6A and is 0-3 in Prep Bowls. Felton is committed to North Dakota as a linebacker.

Caden Gutzmer, QB, Minnetonka. Gutzmer has thrown for 2,193 yards and has led Minnetonka's late-season run. He is committed to North Dakota.

Theo Brown, WR, Minnetonka. Brown is an eighth-grader, and last week, he caught three passes for 70 yards and one touchdown in the semifinal win against Rosemount.

9-Player: Border West vs. Hills-Beaver Creek, 10 a.m.

Owen Deal, QB, and Dylan Groebner, RB, Border West . The co-op formed in 2023 and is already in a state final. Groebner plays both ways and is the player to watch.

Karson Metzger, WR, Hill-Beaver Creek. Metzger caught four passes for 127 yards and two touchdowns in the semifinal against Cromwell-Wright Area.

Brayden Foust, RB, Pierz. Foust has 31 rushing touchdowns. He leads a team that has outscored its 12 opponents 652-76 and is 4-0 all-time in the Prep Bowl.

Samuel Selthun, RB, Waseca. Selthun had 139 rushing yards and one touchdown in the semifinal win against Dilworth-Glyndon-Felton

Class 5A: Mankato West vs. Cretin-Derham Hall, 4 p.m.

Osborne Lorenz, QB, Mankato West . Lorenz is a Mr. Football finalist trying to bring the Scarlets their sixth state title and first since 2021.

Gavin Russell, QB, Cretin-Derham Hall. Russell has thrown 34 touchdown passes, mostly to receivers Antonio Barajas and De'mandre Frierson-Hollie. Both teams are 12-0. CDH is chasing its first title since 2009 under second-year coach Kim Royston, a former Gophers defensive back.
