articles.title: World Chess Championship Round 1: How Gukesh won 'psychologically' in 38-move draw over Javokhir Sindarov
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Sindarov has a 60 min advantage over Gukesh.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Sindarov has a 60 min advantage over Gukesh. What did Gukesh’s team do all this time for the last 2 years?" A random post on X was enough to gauge the tension in the air as two 20-year-old prodigies, Javokhir Sindarov and Dommaraju Gukesh, locked horns in a taut, high-wire curtain-raiser at the 2026 World Chess Championship in Cologny, Switzerland.Minutes later, another screenshot made the rounds. It was not fake or AI-generated. By move 17, the reigning world champion, with Black, was staring at a dwindling 29:51 on his clock, while his Uzbek challenger sat comfortably behind a fortress of over an hour and eighteen minutes.Before move 40, there is no increment, and the math seemed brutal as the titleholder was already staring down the barrel of severe time trouble.Blitzing through the opening stages to turn the clock into a weapon has become Sindarov’s calling card. Earlier this year in Cyprus, wielding the very same high-tempo blueprint, the Uzbek grandmaster tore through the Candidates field like a whirlwind.On Tuesday, playing with the white pieces, which gives the first-move advantage, he looked poised to run that exact playbook once again.Asked afterwards about the ticking clock, Gukesh replied, "I thought I was always under control, or at least not in a place where I really needed to be worried... I was happy that I managed to spend some time and find a good solution (to the opening problems)!"How the game unfoldedThe battle took place in a famous chess setup known as the Berlin Endgame, a notoriously solid, defensive strategy where the queens are traded off early.While it is usually a safe choice, Gukesh rarely plays it, which raised eyebrows.Sindarov wasted no time taking the game into uncharted territory, playing a surprise knight move on turn 13 (13. Ne4) that had never been seen in a top-level in-person tournament before.As Dutch Grandmaster Anish Giri noted in his post-game breakdown, the players skipped the usual middle part of a chess game entirely, jumping straight into a tense, high-stakes endgame."White has a lot of initiative... very dangerous position for Black," Giri said on his YouTube channel.Sindarov's pieces were swarming forward, while one of Gukesh's most powerful pieces, his rook in the corner, remained trapped and unable to join the fight.Forced onto the back foot and burning precious minutes to calculate every danger, Gukesh found a clever defensive setup on moves 17 and 18 (17...Bb4 and 18...h6).By pinning Sindarov’s pieces in place and blocking his path forward, the Indian champion brought White’s attack to a grinding halt.Sindarov still held a slight edge and could have kept building the pressure slowly. Instead, on move 24, he pushed a pawn forward aggressively (24. f4), triggering a fast trade of pieces that accidentally gave Gukesh the escape route he needed.Gukesh responded with cold-blooded accuracy, giving up a pawn to free his king and finally bring his trapped corner rook into the action."All Black's other pieces are good, but the rook on h8 is not in the game," Giri observed. "As soon as the king was able to move up and connect these rooks, bring this rook into play... the opening was essentially over."Once Gukesh’s army was working together, the danger disappeared.In fact, Sindarov had to make one very careful defensive move late in the game to avoid falling into a trap, before forcing a draw by repeating the same moves three times, a standard way chess games end in a tie when neither side can make progress.Neither player made a single major mistake across all 38 moves.Praise from top GrandmastersThe high-wire accuracy drew immediate acclaim from fellow grandmasters on X.Grandmaster Srinath Narayanan wrote: "High quality game one, fitting of a world championship match. Love the amount of watching and interest, again fitting of a world championship match!"Grandmaster Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa posted, "Incredible 1st game of World Championship match! High quality game from both! Gukesh found great moves under pressure! Excited to follow game 2"Grandmaster Vidit Gujrathi also joined in, adding, "A very high quality game considering the pressure of an opening round match. Sindarov showed a new opening idea but Gukesh found good moves, although he was dangerously low on time at some point. articles.body: LSU’s first regular season under Lane Kiffin wraps up on Saturday when the Tigers face Arkansas in Fayetteville. A football season that could end with no more than seven wins, amid controversy over the eligibility of former NFL players, has fallen well short of what LSU likely hoped for. But an even greater disappointment could be looming in Baton Rouge. According to an amended complaint filed Monday in federal court in Alabama, the SEC has threatened to put LSU’s possible expulsion from the conference to a vote. Commissioner Greg Sankey has scheduled another special meeting for Dec. 3, "to consider the termination of LSU's membership in the SEC." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE If the vote takes place, LSU’s fate would rest with the conference’s chancellors and presidents. Whether the school broke the conference's policies on professionalism on former NFL players has been called into question. However, LSU’s issues extend to its basketball program, where former NBA players have been added to the roster. Former St. John’s player RJ Luis Jr. appeared in preseason games with the Boston Celtics last season. He played in one game for the Tigers, scoring 11 points ina a 79-67 Tigers win over Louisiana-Monroe last Wednesday. Shortly after the game, LSU President Wade Rousse said he told Tigers basketball coach Will Wade should not take the court in future games. LSU POKED THE SEC BEAR, THEN FOLDED: RJ LUIS BENCHED AFTER CONFERENCE LEADERS DISCUSSED EXPULSION OR BOYCOTT In an affidavit, Sankey said the conference will consider expelling LSU regardless of whether Luis remains sidelined. NFL rules analyst Terry McAulay weighed in and offered a blunt criticism of his alma mater’s coaching decisions and alleged conference-rule violations. "LSU is my alma mater. articles.title: World Chess Championship: Sindarov says 'Indian chess players are always meditating' after first game draw with Gukesh
articles.summary: Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov made an interesting observation about Indian chess players when asked about the psychological state of his opponent, D
articles.body: Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov made an interesting observation about Indian chess players when asked about the psychological state of his opponent, D Gukesh, after their opening game of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva ended in a drwa on Tuesday. "I saw that all the players from India are always meditating," Sindarov said, adding that he had noticed the habit while playing against Gukesh, R Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi.The remark came during the post-match press conference after defending champion Gukesh, playing with black, drew the first game against the Uzbek challenger. The two players were also asked about how they read each other's behaviour at the board, with Sindarov pointing to Gukesh closing his eyes and Indian players meditating."I do it in every tournament; it's not just here. And also, I saw that all the players from India are always meditating, which for me is okay. I played many times with Arjun, Pragg, and Gukesh; maybe not many, but whenever we meet, he is also meditating. So nothing special here," Sindarov said.Gukesh, meanwhile, said the two players had similar habits and that their actions at the board were not necessarily signs of nerves."I don't know, maybe there were a little bit of nerves also, but I think both of our habits are similar. In general, he taps his foot or shakes his leg, and I close my eyes, in any tournament, not just the match. It's just how we behave at the board," the Indian said.On the board, Gukesh had to work his way back after Sindarov gained a small advantage in the early stages. The Indian chose the Berlin Defence against Sindarov's Ruy Lopez, and was under some pressure before the game moved into a queen-less middle game.Sindarov had better-placed pieces and a slightly better pawn structure for a period, but the Uzbek sacrificed a pawn to open up the position. Gukesh, however, found the right moves despite being short of time. At one point, the Indian appeared to have a chance to take control, but Sindarov held his position and repeated the moves.The position was repeated five times before the players agreed to a draw. A threefold repetition is usually enough to claim a draw.Asked how it felt to finally play after all the build-up to the championship, Gukesh said the actual game was the easiest part of the process."That was the easiest thing, to actually go and play the game, because there's so much thinking, so much work to do before that. Once you get to the game, you know, it's like your home."He also said he was not worried despite getting into time trouble, as he had already considered his next moves."I thought I was always under control, not in a place where I really needed to be worried. When I got into time trouble, I had already thought about the next few moves, what I was going to play soon. I was happy that I managed to spend some time, find a good solution, and the moves after that were pretty easy."The two players will contest 14 classical games, with the first to reach 7.5 points winning the title. If the scores are level after 14 games, shorter-format games will be played to decide the champion. Gukesh will have the white pieces in the second game.The time control allows 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, with 30 seconds added for every move from move 41. Players cannot agree to a draw before 40 moves, although a game can end earlier through threefold repetition or stalemate.The total prize fund for the match is USD 2.5 million. Each win is worth USD 200,000, with the remaining amount to be split equally between the players. If the match goes to tie-breaks, the winner will receive USD 1.3 million and the runner-up USD 1.2 million.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Urban Meyer reveals his pick for the Big Ten’s top team ahead of College Football Playoff
articles.summary: Urban Meyer says the Oregon Ducks are the Big Ten's best team despite an 8-3 season, calling the conference's College Football Playoff outlook shaky.
articles.body: College football’s rivalry week is here. Ohio State, the 2024 College Football Playoff national champion, will host Michigan on Saturday. Elsewhere in the Big Ten, crosstown rivals UCLA and USC will meet at the historic Rose Bowl in Pasadena. The Big Ten has produced the past three national champions, but this year’s conference appears to lack a team that clearly stands above the rest. Urban Meyer, who coached Ohio State to a national championship in 2014, offered his take on the conference’s best team. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "I see Oregon as the best team in the Big Ten Conference," Meyer said on The Triple Option podcast. "Followed by Indiana, because of defense and because of culture there. And then, I got a dotted line. Iowa and UCLA below them." The latest CFP rankings had UCLA as the lone Big Ten team in the top 10 at No. 9. The Bruins had been ranked in the top five before suffering their first loss Saturday. Their playoff hopes took another hit when quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was injured in the overtime loss to Michigan. Nico Iamaleava, UCLA’s opening-day starter, was injured Oct. 11 and later ruled out for the season. TENNESSEE JUMPS, ALABAMA DROPS, INDIANA AND UCLA TUMBLE IN NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF TOP 25 POLL Indiana, the defending national champions, fell to 9-2 last week after an upset loss to Washington. Despite those setbacks, Meyer does not believe the Big Ten will only send one team to the playoffs. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "There's no chance," Meyer said. "I shouldn't say there's no chance. If the Big Ten gets blown apart again like it did last week, possibly. But no, there's not." The Big Ten’s recent run of success has raised questions about whether the SEC’s longtime reign as college football’s top conference has ended. Meyer acknowledged that the SEC is at the top of the sport, at least for now. "The SEC is superior to the Big Ten this year. It's not close this year. It's not," Meyer continued. "Just watch the film. The speed, athleticism, you're going to see more draft picks in the SEC again, like old school. You just don't see that in the Big Ten." COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S QUIET SATURDAY TURNS INTO A BIG TEN DISASTER WITH BRUTAL CFP CONSEQUENCES But, Meyer still believes Oregon is the one Big Ten team capable of matching the SEC’s talent. "You do see that from Oregon. When you push play on Oregon, you see the speed, athleticism, and size that you see in the SEC. You do not see that in Indiana. Not on offense. On defense, you do." articles.title: Parris Mason: New Zealand netball league collapse leaves players in limbo
articles.summary: Parris Mason on concerns about her netball future after the collapse of the domestic league in New Zealand.
articles.body:
All Parris Mason has known is playing netball. But with a World Cup just nine months away, she and four other New Zealand players have been left in limbo after the collapse of their domestic league.

"There's a high potential I will not be playing netball heading into a World Cup," she told BBC Sport.

While a significant number of her Silver Ferns team-mates play professionally in Australia and England, Mason stayed with her home league.

The 23-year-old defender, who has been a full-time professional for six years, found out her netball fate when the news was leaked to the media.

"It shattered me," she said. "The influx of emotions; is my career over? What do I do next? It was just so much to handle all at once."

Netball New Zealand admitted the way events unfolded publicly was deeply regrettable and has pledged to support the affected players.

"We know this period of uncertainty has been extremely tough for players, coaches, teams and everyone involved in the domestic competition," a statement said.

"Their wellbeing is our priority, and we are working closely with the New Zealand Netball Players' Association to support them."

It comes as the Silver Ferns are on the cusp of becoming the world's number one ranked side, after winning gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and beating Australia in the Constellation Cup.

The World Cup will be held in Sydney, Australia, between 25 August and 5 September, with New Zealand looking to win the title for a sixth time.

There had been uncertainty over the future of the ANZ Premiership for a couple years. The league had struggled to secure long-term broadcast deals which impacted the league financially.

In 2026, the league recorded a loss of around $NZ 3.7m (£1.5m). There was an exodus of the country's best players.

Ten of the 12 Silver Ferns who won gold for New Zealand at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow have moved overseas to play - primarily in Australia.

Businesswoman Anna Mowbray and her husband, former All Blacks player Ali Williams, pitched a new private league for 2027, but negotiations fell through just eight weeks after signing a term sheet.

"I don't understand my life without netball," said Mason. "It's been a big part of my identity, and [there is a] mental toll to [being] continually knocked down.

"I think of everything in this whole situation as just completely sad."

Nathan Limm, who has been following the story for the New Zealand Herald said: "The Ferns' success feels a little bit fragile. They get a few injuries, where's the depth underneath if they're not playing domestic netball?

"The communication between Netball NZ and the Players Association, with their investors, with the public, has been so rocky.

"I think there is a real distinct lack of trust between the players and Netball NZ."

When asked whether there are plans for a domestic netball competition next season New Zealand Netball said: "Work on an elite domestic competition for 2027 is well under way. Our goal is a sustainable, professional competition for 2027 and beyond."

articles.summary: Imma Roquet, Claudio Castilla y Antonio Pérez llegan a esta cita tras proclamarse campeones de España en sus respectivas disciplinas: salto de obstáculos, doma clásica y enganches
articles.body: Mutua Madrid Horse Week 2026 reunirá del 26 al 29 de noviembre en IFEMA Madrid a tres de los grandes protagonistas del panorama ecuestre nacional. Imma Roquet, Claudio Castilla y Antonio Pérez llegarán a la cita madrileña tras conquistar el oro en sus respectivos Campeonatos de España de 2026, representando a las tres disciplinas que protagonizan el programa deportivo del evento: salto de obstáculos, doma clásica y enganches. Tres disciplinas con características y exigencias muy diferentes, pero que comparten un mismo denominador: la compenetración entre caballo y deportista, el trabajo constante y la búsqueda de la excelencia deportiva. En salto de obstáculos, Imma Roquet llegará a Madrid tras proclamarse campeona de España absoluta en 2026. La amazona catalana, una de las representantes destacadas del panorama ecuestre nacional, tendrá la oportunidad de medirse a algunas de las principales figuras internacionales de la disciplina en una edición que volverá a situar el Longines FEI Jumping World Cup™ en el centro de la competición. En doma clásica, Claudio Castilla también estará presente tras conquistar el oro en el Campeonato de España Absoluto de 2026. El jinete español representará a nuestro país en una de las disciplinas más técnicas y elegantes de la hípica, donde la precisión, la armonía y la conexión entre caballo y jinete son fundamentales. Su participación contribuirá a dar protagonismo a la doma nacional en un programa que contará con la celebración de la FEI Dressage World Cup. Por su parte, Antonio Pérez de Pedrajas llegará a Mutua Madrid Horse Week como campeón de España de enganches 2026 en la categoría de cuartas. La coincidencia de estos tres campeones nacionales en una misma edición refleja la diversidad y el nivel del deporte ecuestre español. Salto, doma y enganches compartirán escenario con algunas de las grandes figuras internacionales, en cuatro jornadas en las que Madrid volverá a convertirse en punto de encuentro de la hípica mundial. articles.title: María Aperador, experta en ciberseguridad, explica cómo evitar que accedan a tu WhatsApp por el buzón de voz: “Activa la verificación en dos pasos”
articles.standfirst: Esto es lo que debes hacer para que nadie entre a tu perfil en la app de mensajería
articles.summary: Esto es lo que debes hacer para que nadie entre a tu perfil en la app de mensajería
articles.body: Hoy en día es prácticamente imposible encontrar a alguien que no use, a lo largo del día, la aplicación de mensajería WhatsApp. Sin embargo, no todos conocen a fondo los fallos de seguridad y los problemas que puedes tener cuando la empleas, ya que existen muchas bandas criminales dedicadas a la estafa y que tratan de acceder a tu perfil para lograr tus datos e información sensible. María Aperador, experta en ciberseguridad, acaba de compartir un interesante consejo para evitar uno de los métodos más efectivos de estos grupos: entrar a tu WhatsApp a través del buzón de voz. “Te pueden robar el WhatsApp sin tocar tu móvil: a través del buzón de voz. Lleva semanas pasando en México, Perú y Paraguay, y el INCIBE ya avisó de esto en España”, aclara. Ante esto, indica que el primer paso para lograr que los ciberdelincuentes no accedan a tu perfil es activar la verificación en dos pasos, debiendo entrar a tus ajustes y luego hacer clic sobre ‘Cuenta’. Tras esto, debes pedir a tu compañía telefónica que desactive tu buzón de voz si no lo sueles usar. Aperador cuenta que, si lo usas, en ese caso debes ponerle “una clave que no sea 1234 ni tu fecha de nacimiento”. “Nunca le des a nadie un código de WhatsApp. Si te llegan códigos que no has pedido, alguien lo está intentando”, explica la experta en ciberseguridad. Para Aperador, el buzón de voz “es la puerta de entrada” a tu smartphone y no hace ninguna falta que lo toquen para acceder. “Mucho cuidado”, avisa. Algunos usuarios se han hecho eco de este tipo de sucesos y han revelado que en otros países como Colombia también está ocurriendo. “Qué tiempos tan malos vivimos”, subrayan sobre este tipo de problemas en la app de mensajería.

articles.title: Thanksgiving sports guide: The best NFL and NBA games to watch this week
articles.summary: If you are looking to avoid an awkward social interaction this Thanksgiving holiday or you have simply eaten so much food your only option is to sit on the couch, there will be a buffet of sports options to keep your mind occupied this week.
articles.body: If you are looking to avoid an awkward social interaction this Thanksgiving holiday or you have simply eaten so much food your only option is to sit on the couch, there will be a buffet of sports options to keep your mind occupied this week. Between some of the best NFL matchups of the season and some high-stakes NBA showdowns, the drama on the court and field should be as delicious as your favorite side dish. (Or equally juicy as the gossip about that one cousin the rest of your family talks about behind their back.) Here’s your viewing guide for which sports to watch over the Thanksgiving break. Wednesday, Nov. 25 Miami Heat vs. Philadelphia 76ers When and where: 5 p.m. ET, ESPN This is the first meeting between two teams that completely overhauled their rosters in the offseason. Several MVPs and Finals MVPs will be on the floor, from the Heat’s Giannis Antentokounmpo to the 76ers’ LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown. Philadelphia has started the season 14-4, while Miami will enter riding high on a seven-game win streak. Adding another sprinkle of sage over the top? James considered a reunion with the Heat in the summer before ultimately choosing the Sixers. Green Bay Packers vs. Los Angeles Rams When and where: 8 p.m. ET, Netflix The NFL is trying to make fetch happen with a new Thanksgiving eve game, and the league is going all out by putting two Super Bowl contenders in this newly devised television slot. After a rocky 2-4 start to the season, the Rams have won four in a row, finally living up to their lofty preseason expectations. The Packers are coming off a loss but will be receiving a shot in the arm thanks to the return of star pass rusher Micah Parsons, playing in his first game since tearing his ACL last season. Expect great quarterback play and hungry defenses in this one. Thursday, Nov. 26 Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions When and where: 1 p.m. ET, CBS The Thanksgiving NFL slate kicks off with a matchup carrying massive implications for the rest of the season. The Bears and Lions are both 8-2, tied at the top of the ultra-competitive NFC North. The winner gets a significant leg up at hosting a playoff game and staying in the race for the conference’s No. 1 seed, while the loser will drop into a crowded field of wild-card hopefuls. If you find yourself feeling sleepy, the explosive offenses in this game will provide a stronger jolt than anything you can find in a cup. Philadelphia Eagles vs. Dallas Cowboys When and where: 4:30 p.m. ET, Fox This game lost quite a bit of luster thanks to the season-ending injury to Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts. Both teams are entering with records under .500, though the Cowboys have at least played an entertaining brand of football this year. If there’s one game to skip if you want to pretend you’re prioritizing your loved ones, it’s probably this one. Kansas City Chiefs vs. Buffalo Bills When and where: 8:20 p.m., NBC Folks, it does not get better than this. The 8-2 Chiefs take on the 9-1 Bills on a cold and rainy night in Buffalo in the latest chapter of the NFL’s best current quarterback rivalry. Both Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen have played like possible MVPs this season, and both their teams are in a race for the top seed in the AFC. It’s possible, perhaps even likely, that whoever wins this one hosts the inevitable rematch in the AFC Championship game. Save room for leftovers, make yourself another plate and cherish the fact you’ll get to watch this game warm and secure from the comfort of a couch. Friday, Nov. 27 Denver Broncos vs. Pittsburgh Steelers When and where: 3 p.m. ET, Prime Video The NFL’s Black Friday game is back, and it features an 8-2 Broncos team taking on the 6-4 Steelers. Pittsburgh has dropped two straight, and has now benched four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph set to start as quarterback. Miami Heat vs. New York Knicks When and where: 7 p.m. ET, Prime Video After taking Thursday off, the NBA returns Friday with a full slate, including this tantalizing matchup between the Heat and the Knicks. It will be Giannis and Co.’s first chance at taking on the defending champs, and should go a long way in telling us if Miami is to be taken seriously as a title threat. Los Angeles Lakers vs. San Antonio Spurs When and where: 9:30 p.m. ET, Prime Video This may be the best game of the entire week in any sport. The historic Western Conference rivals will square off for the first time this season and will feature the NBA’s clear-cut, top-two MVP candidates: the Lakers’ Luka Doncic and the Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama. Doncic is averaging a comical 36.6 points per game this season, while Wembanyama is not far behind at 29.9 points a night in addition to his freakish defense. This showdown features the game’s best offensive engine going against the game’s best defensive force. Expect both to try to make a statement.

The Tigers forfeited most of last season after injuries and roster depth forced them to the sidelines.

These teams started playing in 2010. Rogers had played De La Salle from 1926-1970 and Tiverton battled Warren from 1970-1992. Both of those opposing schools closed and the Vikings and Tigers both faced other opponents before settling on one another. Thursday's game will be at Tiverton High School.

articles.title: Lincoln sack head coach duo Cohen and Shaw
articles.summary: Lincoln sack head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side.
articles.body:
Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side.

The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday.

The loss leaves the Imps just three points above the relegation places in what is the club's first season back in the second tier for 65 years.

Cohen and Shaw were assistant coaches under Michael Skubala when Lincoln were promoted as League One title winners last season.

They were surprisingly promoted to replace their boss as a joint managerial double act.

The duo oversaw just four wins from 17 league games this season, and Tuesday's loss at The Valley was their fifth in succession and heaviest since being thumped 6-0 by West Ham in mid-October.

Lincoln's chairman Ron Fowler, the American billionaire who took a controlling stake in the club when they were on their way to promotion last season, said the decision to sack the pair was in the "best interests" of the Imps.

"We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division," he told the club website.

First-team coach Shaun Pearson will take charge of Lincoln, with the support of Paul McShane and David Preece, on an interim basis.

Lincoln are next in action on Saturday when they host high-flying Wolves.

articles.body:
Lincoln City have sacked head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw after only six months in charge of the Championship club.

So Lincoln fans, is this the right decision and why has the appointment not worked out?

Who should the Imps be looking to in their search to replace Cohen and Shaw, to stand a realistic chance of staying in the Championship?

Send us your thoughts here and check back later to read some of the views of Lincoln supporters.

articles.title: Top Florida high school football playoff regional championship games
articles.summary: Choctaw and St. Augustine meet for the fifth consecutive season, while rivals Eau Gallie and Merritt Island play for the fourth time in 13 months.
articles.body:
Other than the state championship games, perhaps no round of the FHSAA football playoffs is more talked about or anticipated than the regional championships.

Maybe it's the cliches of no practice feels better than Thanksgiving morning or Thanksgiving dinner tastes better after practice, but this round just has a certain prestige.

Oh yeah, it's also the gateway to the state semifinals and this year provides fans with some intriguing matchups.

Lake Mary, which won the Class 7A state championship in 2025 , travels to DeLand . Lake Mary won just two games in the regular season but has won back-to-back regional playoff games, including a 40-0 rout of No. 1 Seminole. Lake Mary beat DeLand in the 2025 regional final, but DeLand shut out Lake Mary on Sept. 11.

Other rematches of 2025 regional championships include Buchholz at Mandarin and Choctawhatchee at St. Augustine .

Here's a look at some of the top regional championships to watch on Friday, Nov. 27:

Buchholz (11-1) is attempting to win its sixth consecutive regional championship. That streak includes beating Mandarin 27-20 in the 2025 Region 1-6A final in Gainesville. The Bobcats scored 13 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to beat Nease 32-31 in the regional semifinals last week . Junior quarterback Andrew Whittemore threw for 139 yards and rushed 24 times for 132 yards and four touchdowns. Mandarin (11-1) has won its two regional playoff games by a combined score of 90-13. Mandarin senior running back Shaunqueze Foster had 15 carries for 164 yards and four touchdowns in a 45-6 win over Evans in the regional semifinals.

Palmetto is looking for its first regional title since 2020, while Armwood was a Class 6A regional champion in 2025. Palmetto (11-1) beat Tampa Bay Tech 12-9 in the regional semifinals. Kicker Brandin Gallaway, who flipped his commitment from Clemson to Tennessee on Nov. 23, connected on four field goals — including a 57-yarder and the game-winner as time expired . Armwood (11-1) is undefeated in Florida this season and has scored at least 37 points in five consecutive games. Hawks sophomore quarterback Kab Nijher completed seven of 18 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in the 37-12 win over Sumner in the regional semifinals.

No. 4 Choctawhatchee at No. 2 St. Augustine

Choctawhatchee and St. Augustine are meeting in the regional playoffs for the fifth consecutive year. The teams split the previous four meetings, with Choctaw winning 31-28 in the regional semifinal in 2025. Choctaw (9-2) is coming off an impressive 32-7 win at top-ranked Columbia in a game played in ankle-deep mud. Senior Dante Whidbee led the Indians with 114 rushing yards, while senior Carter Marracco had a pair of rushing touchdowns. St. Augustine (11-1) has won all seven home games this season . The last time the Yellow Jackets lost at home was against Choctaw in 2025. St. Augustine junior Mason Beane had 14 tackles and two tackles for loss in a 29-0 win over Rickards in the regional semifinal.

Jones has won five consecutive regional championships and reached the Class 4A state championship the past two seasons. Vanguard is aiming for its first regional title since 2023. Jones beat Vanguard in the regional playoffs in each of the past two seasons. Jones (9-3) has won of its past six, including a 16-13 overtime win over Lake Wales in the regional semifinal. Vanguard (10-2) has won nine in a row and has scored least 21 points in every game this season. The Knights scored 41 points in the second half of its 54-34 road win at No. 1 Bishop Moore in the regional semifinal. Senior quarterback Terrance Lewis threw for 192 yards and a touchdown and rushed for 207 yards and four scores in the win.

These rivals are playing for the fourth time in 13 months. Eau Gallie swept both meetings in 2025, including a regional semifinal win. Merritt Island won the regular season game on Oct. 9, beating the Commodores 36-35 in overtime on the road. Eau Gallie (8-4) topped previously undefeated Villages Charter 42-35 in the regional semifinal. Sophomore running back X'Zavier Corbin had a career game with 21 carries for 321 yards and two touchdowns. Merritt Island (12-0) has a potent offense that is averaging 45.25 points per game and has scored at least 35 points in every game. Mustangs senior quarterback Kevin Verpaele (USF commit) completed 11 of 13 passes for 305 yards and five touchdowns and rushed for 48 yards and a score against Santa Fe in the regional semifinal.

Clearwater Central Catholic at The First Academy

This is one of the best matchups in the state from a MaxPreps perspective. The First Academy (9-3) was in the Open Division mix for most of the season and finished No. 13 in Florida, one spot ahead of Clearwater Central Academy (10-2). Both teams have cruised through the first two rounds of the regional playoffs. TFA freshman running back Hyquez Russell had 18 carries for 168 yards and two touchdowns against Tampa Catholic last week. CCC avenged a regular season loss in its 35-7 win over Berkeley Prep in the semifinal. Senior quarterback Khayse Barrett completed 13 of 15 passes for 89 yards and a touchdown and rushed for 135 yards and a touchdown in the win.

University Christian at Trinity Christian

See the photos as University Christian, Trinity football face off

This is a rematch of Trinity's 14-8 regular season win on Aug. 28 . That was a dramatic and very strange showdown that featured almost 20 penalties, weather delays, clock issues and a bizarre goal line stand as time expired by Trinity's defense. Trinity (8-4) has won five games in a row. Conquerors quarterbacks Terel Dallas and Hicks Zarah combined to throw for 308 yards and three touchdowns against Melbourne Central Catholic in the regional semifinal. University (9-3) topped previously undefeated Hawthorne 20-0 in the regional semifinal. Senior running back Kyree Wilson averaged 120.2 yards per game and scored 15 touchdowns through his first 10 games of the season.

articles.title: North Jersey Female Athlete of the Week helped usher in a golden era
articles.summary: Lizzie Rubin is the NorthJersey.com Female Athlete of the Week, presented by HSS.
articles.body:
Lizzie Rubin sees things on a soccer field that most players don't.

She can spot a passing lane before it opens, switch the field with a perfect diagonal ball and anticipate how to break up an opponent's counter.

Yet ask coach Drew Strohmeyer what he'll remember most about the Princeton commit, and the conversation quickly goes beyond technique.

"The best leader I've ever coached," Strohmeyer said. "She is the real deal. Just the way she carries herself on and off the field, it's different. It's like having a coach out on the field."

That leadership helped usher in a golden era.

A few years ago, Ramsey was still chasing the milestones that now seem routine. The Rams had not won a state championship in more than a decade. They had never won a Bergen County title and had never cracked the national rankings.

By the time Rubin stepped off the bus Saturday night, she had changed all that.

The Princeton commit closed her high school career with 65 goals and 80 assists while helping Ramsey compile an 89-5-1 record over four seasons. During that span, the Rams won three state titles and two Bergen County crowns, transforming one of North Jersey's most respected programs into something greater.

Her last high school game was a fitting end. Rubin set up two goals, both off corner kicks, as Ramsey beat Delsea, 3-0, in the Group 2 final.

Hours later, the celebration stretched through town.

Police cars, fire trucks and ambulances escorted Ramsey home while residents lined the streets to cheer.

"It was the coolest thing ever," said Rubin, the North Jersey Female Athlete of Week, presented by HSS.

A natural midfielder who typically plays a deeper role for powerhouse club PDA, Rubin became the point guard of Ramsey's offense. She finished with 20 goals and a state-leading 33 assists this season while taking all the set pieces.

Then there was the captain's work off the field.

Strohmeyer recalled a state tournament practice last season when a younger player arrived late and visibly upset after oversleeping.

Before the coach could finish reassuring the player that everything was fine, Rubin had already peeled away from the group, put her arm around her teammate and made sure she felt OK.

Rubin's connection to the Ramsey program goes way back. Her older sister, Katie, was a three-time All-County center back who played two seasons alongside her in high school. Rubin also credits her parents, particularly her father, Daniel, for developing her game.

"My dad has been one of the biggest influences on my soccer career," Rubin said. "We're always out training together. He's pushing me, watching film, just helping me in any way that he can. He loves it just as much as I do. It's the same thing with my mom. She's involved as well. She's more of my support system."

Meet the North Jersey Athletes of the Week for 2026-27 season

In September, Rubin suffered an MCL sprain that threatened to sidetrack her senior year. But Rubin missed only two games and felt back to 100 percent about two weeks after returning.

By season's end, Rubin had not only returned to form but earned All-American honors for a team that went 22-1.

As the clock wound down Saturday, Rubin found herself trying to absorb every second.

Hope Ernst ran over and embraced her. Then came Kendall Reid, Kate Schwanewede and Julia Bauer, friends she'd been playing with since she was 6 years old with the Ramsey Hotspurs.

"That was when it really hit me," Rubin said. "I was like, wow, this is an unforgettable season. I can't believe it's over."

Soon, Rubin will head to Princeton and begin a new chapter. She will likely pursue a path in business and economics.

Before she does, there will be one more decision to make. The Ramsey captains will get to design their state rings and add another symbol to the most successful era in program history.

An era that, in many ways, will forever be tied to Rubin.

Accomplishment : Rubin finished with two assists on Saturday in Ramsey's 3-0 win over Delsea in the Group 2 final. She had one assist in the state semifinal earlier in the week.

articles.title: How to buy Tennessee Titans chairback seats, memorabilia from Nissan Stadium
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans fans can now purchase original Nissan Stadium memorabilia, like chairback seats. Here's how to buy them.
articles.body:
Want to own a drink coaster made of turf from the original Nissan Stadium?

Tennessee Titans fans can start buying Nissan Stadium seats , chairbacks and other memorabilia for later pickup, the team announced Nov. 24, with proceeds benefitting youth programming in Tennessee through the Tennessee Titans Foundation.

The Titans have been in the current Nissan Stadium since 1999. They will begin playing in the new Nissan Stadium in 2027 when new construction east of the original site is complete.

The team announced its sale in July but there was no point of purchase until now.

Chair seatbacks from the original stadium, minus the seats, start at $79.99 with discounts available to season ticket holders through Jan. 3. Seats and select turf products are available for in-person pickup in late January 2027 or can be shipped for a fee.

New Nissan Stadium tour: See latest construction at Tennessee Titans new field

Portions of artificial turf, goalposts and "other unique items" from the Titans' home stadium since 1999 will go on sale. Current listed items include plaques with pieces of yellow goalposts mounted in them ($99) and doormats ($99) made of the field's turf.

Price points are as high as $599.99 for connected full chairback seats with the Titans logo . Fans have the option to pay for personalized seats with their name, row and seat number.

Certificates of authenticity, as well as a QR-coded hologram with information about the item, come with each purchase. The Titans are collaborating with CollectibleXchange, the company that led similar memorabilia projects after the removal of Yankee Stadium and Texas Stadium.

"We understand that these items represent so much more than concrete, steel or seats,"CollectibleXchange owner Brandon Steiner said in a release. "They represent the players, the games, the traditions and the countless memories that have made this stadium home to generations of Titans fans."

articles.title: Moving the chains: Female tackle football player flourishes on the field
articles.summary: Huckeby joined the women’s professional tackle football team during the 2026 season, became a starter and played every offensive snap in game action.
articles.body:
The Indiana Valor offense huddled up during a practice at Greenwood Fieldhouse. With her glasses slipping slightly off her nose and an American flag mouthguard in place, center Bonnie Huckeby led the women's professional tackle football team through its next play, snapping the ball to her quarterback.

The 30-year-old has spent her entire life leading and helping others. As a former softball player and coach, powerlifter and dedicated community member, being named a captain in her first year with the Valor felt like a natural fit.

"I lead from beside, not from in front of or behind," she said. "I'm going to go through the trenches with you. Like, we're going to get through it together."

Huckeby joined the team during the 2026 season, and became a starter and playing every offensive snap in game action. But training hasn't been easy as a mom, a wife and a full-time employee in hospice care.

The team practices twice a week during the season, and Huckeby does two to three additional workouts a week when she can find the time.

See Indy women's professional tackle football team's starting center in action

"I really don't have a schedule," she said. "It's when can I fit this workout in? Is it going to be at home? Is it going to be at the gym? Obviously, things are chaotic, but I still make it happen."

Amid the chaos, Huckeby said she and her teammates are extremely supportive of one another because they share daily obstacles of motherhood and being an athlete.

"I don't think there's anybody better for the sport of football than a mom, especially for offense," she said. "We sacrifice ourselves all for the better of our team. That's what a mom does. You're sacrificing yourself, your body, everything that you do for your children. So, it just comes naturally."

With her team alongside her, Huckeby is excited for the future of women's professional football and hopes the league and its players continue to grow and gain respect.

"You should have a full respect for a woman who works 40 hours a week, and is also a mom, and they're also playing professional football on the weekends," she said. "I don't know why anybody wouldn't want to pay to see that.

articles.title: How longtime ESPN reporter beat buzzer for youth sports on 'Jeopardy!'
articles.summary: Jeremy Schaap talks about buzzer techniques, channeling 'useless sports knowledge' for a cause on 'Jeopardy!' and kids' 'essential' right to play.
articles.body:
It was the "Final Jeopardy!" category Jeremy Schaap had to navigate.

It's also the way Schaap, who has been with ESPN for 32 years, felt as a participant of "ESPN Jeopardy!"

"I attach way too much self-esteem, self-regard to knowing pointless trivia," the investigative reporter says. "So for me, this was kind of high stakes because if I didn't win, I would never forgive myself."

The line was said with humor, as much of the friendly banter of competition was over three rounds filmed last spring that debuted in the summer. It was hosted by Joe Buck in the announcer's buddy-buddy style that also jabbed at those he knew.

It had ESPN anchors and hosts as well as actor John Hamm and NFL commentator Kyle Brandt, both of whom faced off with Schaap in the final. Brandt joshed with Schaap about how he elevated his arm out in front of him holding a buzzer when he knew an answer.

"It's intimidating as hell," Brandt said.

In the quarterfinal round, when Schaap faced ESPN's Christine Williamson and Kimberley A. Martin , Martin looked at him and said: "Watched this man my entire life, and I'm determined to take him down because he's one of my idols."

And so it went, as Schaap buzzed and grimaced his way to the inaugural title, but also earned a $500,000 gift for his charity of choice: The International Sports and Music Project (ISMP) . The ISMP is a nonprofit that uses music to create supportive spaces for kids in underserved communities around the world.

"It's easy to take for granted access to sports," Schaap says. "In America it's an issue here as well. We see that sports are becoming more expensive (for) what participation requires now in terms of the efforts from parents and resources and all of that. And it's even less accessible in some of these very poor places around the world where there aren't resources to build fields, to buy equipment, to get the right kind of coaching and mentorship.

"It's absolutely fundamental to development and to physical and emotional well being to have the opportunity to participate in sports."

Schaap, 57, spoke with us about the "Jeopardy!" experience, his career, his views on the youth sports landscape and what his win means for the work of ISMP.

ESPN debuted its version of the timeless game show at the Alex Trebek Stage at Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, California. Longtime narrator Johnny Gilbert announced the contestants. The shows were taped in May and started streaming on the ESPN App, Disney+ and Hulu on July 31.

There were a wide range of contestants across the ESPN landscape and beyond . When Schaap was contacted to participate, he thought he would be on traditional "Jeopardy!" He only realized it was sports-geared on a production call.

"I started studying Shakespeare and Constitutional amendments," he told Buck on he show. "So I prepared for the wrong show."

But when he got on air, he seemed to be a natural at this version.

"I love trivia, so I've been waiting all my life to show off my useless sports knowledge," Schaap told USA TODAY Sports.

The categories ran from traditional ("Mascot Mania" and "Basketball Coaches") to more arcane ("Hey Darnold!" "Nerdy For 30 for 30" and "It's An Antonym…"). The last one was as confusing as it sounded.

"Sammy, the Mascot of UC-Santa Cruz, is this type of slimy creature with a certain amount of appeal," Buck said for the mascot category.

"Uhh, that's so good that you know that," Buck replied with a grin.

Subjects leaned more contemporary in nature – think answers of "Who is Randy Moss?" or "Who is Ja'Marr Chase?" – although Schaap grit his teeth for not being fast enough to answer an Ice Bowl question.

"I was hoping there would be more older stuff, you know pre-1980," Schaap says. "There are a lot of people who are very up on everything that's going on every day now, and certainly a lot of my competitors, but I think I kind of have a good grasp of sports history.

"They asked everybody in the production call what would be your dream category? And I told them, 'Pre-20th century heavyweight champions.' "

Who is Jeremy Schaap and what is his sports history?

Schaap is the son of the late Dick Schaap, a famous sports broadcaster and writer. He wrote books with, among others, Joe Namath, Muhammad Ali and Bo Jackson.

One of Schaap's best friends was Jerry Kramer, the Green Bay offensive lineman and Hall of Famer who is Jeremy's namesake. Kramer made a famous block that secured victory in the Ice Bowl for the Packers over the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 31,1967.

Jeremy Schaap, who was born in 1969, says he knew "from the very beginning" he wanted to be a sports journalist. He met Ali at a golf tournament and Reggie Jackson in the Schaap Manhattan apartment.

"All those guys, they were part of my childhood in a personal way," he says. "My dad was in it and it looked like he was having more fun than anybody else. They had more fun than anybody else's dad as far as I could tell. He loved it and it was exciting and he was around the biggest stars in sports all the time. They were presences in my life, whether he was writing a book with them or just covering them.

"I was like, why would you want to work for a living if you could do this?"

What is Jeremy Schaap's connection to youth sports?

Schaap followed the path of many of us in that his passion for games drove him into adulthood .

"It was such a big part of my childhood, being a sports fan, getting to play, playing in the back alley of where I lived in New York," he says.

He didn't play high school sports but found the contest with colleagues on "Jeopardy!" brought out his competitive side.

"It's nice to have a chance to talk to you because my wife is enforcing a strict no 'Jeopardy!' talk rule," he says.

He says he felt pressure because the folks at ISMP, for whom he serves on the board, were counting on him to win.

"I know that it can go a long way," he says of the $500,000 he won. "That's what I have been told."

According to its website , ISMP has generated more than 1 million individual impact hours through sports, music, mentorship and community programming.

During our interview, Schaap brought up the E:60 episode he did in 2010 about the aftermath of the 1984 gas leak from the Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL) pesticide plant in Bhopal, India. It exposed thousands to toxic chemicals.

"There was nowhere for kids there to play, there were still so many places that had been contaminated by the disaster," Schaap says. "(ISMP) kind of naturally aligns with my interest, and it's not just around the world but also here in the U.S. sports and access to sports is important. And it's important um that we find ways to make it possible for kids to take part and that's a big part of ISMP's mission."

Why aren't more kids playing sports? ESPN devotes $5M to get them back

What are Jeremy Schaap's feelings about youth sports? (And what's the deal with the buzzer on 'Jeopardy!'?)

Schaap, who lives in suburban Connecticut, has three kids (16, 14 and 11) who have been involved in sports.

"Most kids, they're competitive about it or it's about just being healthy," he says. "It's such a great thing and there's so many studies that tie self-esteem, confidence, academic performance to sports participation as well. It's essential, and I think the right to play, it really should be a right rather than a privilege."

Schaap admits he wasn't very good at sports as a kid, but he found himself dueling with Hamm and Brandt in the final.

"The hard thing is kind of just getting your heart rate down," he says. "I was like, 'I drank a bunch of caffeine,' and I was thinking, 'Do I need the energy for the buzzer or should I be at a more even keel?' I couldn't figure it out. I still don't know the answer."

He also credits a chat with ESPN's Mina Kimes, who won "Celebrity Jeopardy!" . Her words of wisdom: It's different on your couch. Trust me.

He also realized contestants can't buzz until after the host finishes asking a question. If you buzz in too soon, you are locked out. He was too eager in earlier rounds and, in the final, he tried a different method with the buzzer.

"Kyle Brandt was upset because he said as soon as he's reading the question, and I felt I knew the answer, I would stick my arm out," he says. "The other guys could see that, and it might have been a little distracting to them. So be it."

Brandt and Hamm, however, were stumped by the "Final Jeopardy!" question that clinched the win for Schaap: "In the past year, this small island became the smallest country to qualify for a FIFA World Cup & got its first MLB Hall of Famer."

"In the moment I wouldn't say it was fun because it felt like a lot of pressure," he says. "But it was fun winning."

Steve Borelli, aka Coach Steve, has been an editor and writer with USA TODAY since 1999. He played baseball in high school, rowed in college and spent 10 years coaching his two sons' baseball and basketball teams. He and his wife, Colleen, are now sports parents to a college and high school baseball player. For his past columns, click here .

Got a question for Coach Steve you want answered in a column? Email him at sborelli@usatoday.com .

articles.title: 3 Reasons Why Ole Miss Football Will Cover the Spread Against Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl
articles.summary: OXFORD, Miss. — The Egg Bowl returns to Oxford on Friday, Nov. 27, as Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State in one of college football’s most heated rivalries. Th...
articles.body:
OXFORD, Miss. — The Egg Bowl returns to Oxford on Friday, Nov. 27, as Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State in one of college football's most heated rivalries.

The Rebels (7-4, 4-4 SEC) enter the contest as substantial favorites against the Bulldogs (5-6, 2-6 SEC). Although rivalry games can produce unexpected results, several factors suggest Ole Miss could win comfortably and cover the spread.

Ole Miss is favored by approximately 17.5 points in early betting markets, although lines vary by sportsbook. Here are three reasons the Rebels are positioned to exceed expectations against their in-state rival.

1. Home-Field Advantage Could Make the Difference

Ole Miss will host the Egg Bowl at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, giving the Rebels a significant advantage in one of the SEC's most emotional rivalry games.

The Rebels have won three consecutive meetings against Mississippi State and five of the last six. Playing in Oxford provides another opportunity to extend that recent dominance.

Moreover, head coach Pete Golding has emphasized the importance of the rivalry throughout the week. Former Ole Miss players addressed the team about the game's significance, helping newcomers understand the stakes.

The Rebels also enter the matchup following a 59-17 victory over Wofford, which provided an opportunity to regain confidence after consecutive SEC defeats.

A strong start could allow Ole Miss to establish control while forcing Mississippi State to play from behind. That scenario would put additional pressure on an already shorthanded Bulldogs offense.

2. Ole Miss Holds a Significant Talent Advantage

Ole Miss possesses the more established offensive personnel, particularly at quarterback and its primary receiving positions.

Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss leads an offense averaging approximately 34.5 points per game. His ability to extend plays and attack defenses through the air creates difficult matchups for opposing secondaries.

The Rebels also feature talented receiving options, including Deuce Alexander and tight end Caleb Odom. Both have contributed to an offense capable of producing explosive plays throughout the season.

Meanwhile, Mississippi State has struggled defensively, particularly against opposing passing attacks. Those difficulties could become more pronounced against Ole Miss' combination of speed and offensive versatility.

The Rebels also benefit from having an experienced coaching staff familiar with the demands of SEC competition.

If Ole Miss executes consistently, its offensive advantages could produce enough scoring opportunities to create separation.

3. Mississippi State Will Be Without Kamario Taylor

Perhaps the most significant factor involves Mississippi State's quarterback situation.

Starting quarterback Kamario Taylor suffered a season-ending injury earlier this season, depriving the Bulldogs of one of their most dynamic offensive players. His absence has limited the offense's ability to threaten opposing defenses with both designed runs and explosive passing plays.

Mississippi State has also dealt with injuries elsewhere in its quarterback room, creating additional challenges for head coach Jeff Lebby.

Without Taylor, the Bulldogs have struggled to sustain the same level of offensive production against SEC opponents.

Ole Miss could exploit that uncertainty by pressuring the quarterback and forcing Mississippi State into difficult passing situations.

Although the Bulldogs still possess talented receivers, including Anthony Evans III, their ability to consistently move the football remains a concern.

If the Rebels establish an early lead, Mississippi State may struggle to generate enough offense to remain within the point spread.

Egg Bowl Prediction: Ole Miss Has the Advantage

The Egg Bowl has produced its share of unexpected results, and Friday's meeting could provide another reminder that records and point spreads mean little in rivalry games.

Mississippi State has additional motivation, needing a victory to reach six wins and become bowl eligible. That urgency should prevent Ole Miss from overlooking its opponent.

However, the Rebels enter with several meaningful advantages, including home-field support, a more established offense and a healthier quarterback situation.

Ole Miss also has an opportunity to close its regular season with eight victories and extend its winning streak against Mississippi State.

The Rebels have the offensive firepower to build a substantial lead, while Mississippi State's quarterback injuries could make a comeback difficult.

Friday's matchup will begin at noon ET on ABC from Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford.

articles.title: 'Random' move has Jacob Murrell flourishing at Falkirk
articles.summary: Jacob Murrell took a big step out of his comfort zone leaving the United States for Falkirk and is enjoying a blistering run of form in Scotland, if not the food.
articles.body:
"It was completely random," is how Jacob Murrell describes his summer switch from DC United to Falkirk.

Now the 22 year-old American is the joint-leading scorer in the Scottish Premiership, with eight goals from 11 starts.

His tremendous form has helped Falkirk surge up the table, with six successive victories taking them from 11th to third place.

"I was looking for more minutes as a young player and Falkirk kind of came out of nowhere," he explained. "They called my agent and a week later I was in Scotland.

"It happened really fast and it was a crazy path to get here. I was just desperate to play. I wasn't happy just being a training player.

"I wanted to win games and score goals and now both are happening."

A Maryland native, the 6ft, 3in centre forward played college football at Georgetown on his way to being a super draft pick for DC United in 2024.

A big Baltimore Ravens fan, Murrell is settling into his new surroundings, although he is wary of the cuisine, telling BBC Scotland he has no plans to try haggis or black pudding.

"The first month was difficult but the club supported me the whole time, making sure I was sound and pushing me to follow my dream.

"Team-mates, staff and fans have all been so good to me and made me feel at home in such a short period of time.

"I grew up north of Baltimore and I'd been in that hour-and-a-half DC radius my entire life with my friends and family, so leaving was really hard.

"Stepping out of my comfort zone has taught me a lot about myself, having to adapt and grow up."

Murrell, the league's player of the month for October, was one of 17 summer signings made by John McGlynn, who ended the club's 15-year absence from the top flight via back-to-back promotions.

"The manager has been so good for me, instilling confidence from day one," he said. "He backs me to score goals and be an influential part of the team."

A first visit to Ibrox is next up for Murrell as Falkirk take on second-placed Rangers on Saturday.

"I'm just taking it day by day, my next focus is Rangers and trying to make it seven on the bounce," he adds.

"Things can turn fast so we need to remember where we came from, stay humble and keep working hard."

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Musiala checked for neurological symptoms in April 2025
articles.summary: Musiala was examined by the German club for neurological dysfunction after the initial onset of symptoms in 2025.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala was first examined for neurological symptoms in April 2025, more than 16 months before the official announcement of the diagnosis by the player, the club has said.

Bayern said they held talks with Musiala’s management team on Tuesday amid speculation about his contract situation following comments by senior club officials over his future and whether he could ever perform again at the highest level.

The comments from honorary president Uli Hoeness and board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, among others, were strongly criticised by the German players’ union.

Musiala, who signed a contract extension to 2030 in February 2025, was diagnosed with a neurological disorder in August after he collapsed in two games and had to be taken off.

“A constructive discussion took place yesterday, Tuesday, between FC Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management,” the club said in a statement.

“For both parties, the player’s health is the absolute priority. Jamal Musiala will receive full support throughout his recovery process.”

“In light of various rumours circulating over the past few days, FC Bayern and 11WINS — the agency representing Jamal — wish to clarify the following: Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025,” Bayern said.

“This examination took place in consultation with FC Bayern and the club’s medical department, immediately following the initial onset of these neurological symptoms.”

Musiala said in August that he had been diagnosed with “temporary, brief, but easily treatable absences caused by a neurological dysfunction”.

Musiala missed much of last season after breaking his leg during the 2025 Club World Cup. In September, he was sidelined with a hamstring injury, returning to action last week in a 1-1 draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga.

articles.title: Senegal deny Morocco’s allegations of ‘contact’ with CAS amid AFCON row
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Senegal were the rightful winners of the 2025 African Cup of Nations.
articles.body:
The president of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), Abdoulaye Fall, has denied Moroccan allegations that he had “contact” with a Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) arbitrator who ruled that Senegal were the rightful winners of the 2025 African Cup of Nations.

The Moroccan federation (FRMF) alleged after Tuesday’s ruling there had been “contact” between Fall and German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three CAS panel members, 48 hours before they decided “unanimously” to award the trophy to Senegal.

“That is absolutely false. I have never had any exchange with any member of CAS,” said Fall on private television channel TFM on Wednesday.

“It surprised and astonished me that such accusations could even be made. I have never been in contact with anyone in connection with this procedure.”

In January, Senegal won a chaotic final 1-0 after extra-time.

But two months later, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless.

The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations.

Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered [loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”.

However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on.

The three-person CAS panel therefore considered the referee’s decision to restart the final showed “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”.

The Moroccan federation has the option of lodging an appeal with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, which does not rule on the merits of the case, but intervenes in procedural matters.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan knocked out by 61-year-old Tony Drago at Snooker 900 Crucible Cup in Reading
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan knocked out by 61-year-old Tony Drago at Snooker 900 Crucible Cup in Reading; O'Sullivan lost 5-3 to the Maltese former professional in second round having lost in the first round in his last three tournaments
articles.body:
O'Sullivan lost 5-3 to the Maltese former professional over a unique format which is played over 15-minute frames under a shot clock.

In a rare appearance in a UK ranking tournament last month, O'Sullivan lost in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open to world number 110 Ka Wai Cheung.

Drago is a former world top 10 player who reached his only ranking tournament final at the 1997 International Open, losing to Stephen Hendry.

Drago's love of the 900 format is perhaps no surprise. He was known for his speed around the table and took just 81 minutes to beat Joe O'Boye 9-0 in the first round of the 1990 UK Championships.

An emotional Drago told Pluto TV: "I thought, I'm going to try my best, and to beat Ronnie O'Sullivan at 61, it's crazy. If you asked me this a few years ago I'd have said, 'leave me alone, you're joking'."

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers released by Steelers after going  scorched earth on coach Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday launched a series of incendiary accusations toward his Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after being benched only a few hours earlier.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday launched a series of incendiary accusations toward his Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after being benched only a few hours earlier. In an interview on ESPN’s “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday, Rodgers accused McCarthy of sleeping through team meetings, missing team meetings and calling the team by the wrong name during a halftime huddle. The veteran quarterback, who said he is not going back to the Steelers, also said McCarthy was “unwell” and should consider letting someone else lead the team going forward. Rodgers is being released by the Steelers after the interview, McCarthy said Wednesday. The accusations leveled by Rodgers have not yet been answered by the Steelers and McCarthy. It’s expected that McCarthy will address the media later on Wednesday. Rodgers burns it down McAfee’s show has become a regular spot for Rodgers to air his grievances and when the show teased a special guest after the news of his surprise benching, the NFL world braced itself. Nobody, however, could have been prepared for what Rodgers – who has said he is retiring after this season – would eventually say. Rodgers started by describing his last week with the Steelers, a week he said summarized what he’s been dealing with this season. “Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring,” Rodgers said “Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again and less than five minutes after that he walks out the room like nothing happened.” Rodgers said the head coach was then absent from an offensive meeting on Thursday before failing to show at a walkthrough on Friday and he then missed a morning meeting on Saturday before the Steelers’ game in Philadelphia. It was during Sunday’s game against the Eagles where Rodgers said McCarthy lost a lot of the team. “I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it … there’s some rambling or something and without even a heads up he says, ‘Alright, 1, 2, 3 Packers,’” Rodgers said. “That’s what he broke it down on in the locker room.” The Steelers went on to lose that game against the Eagles, 19-16, to drop their record to 6-4. ‘A change is needed’ The 42-year-old Rodgers said this has been a situation bubbling under the surface throughout the season and since training camp. “We’ve had these conversations for months now and it began as a concerned friend about somebody who’s unhealthy,” Rodgers said. “If you’re sleeping in meetings, you’re unhealthy, if you’re not coming to everything you should be coming to as a play caller. “How many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff? I gave you one week, I could go week by week throughout the season on stuff that was going on.” There has been no public information on McCarthy’s health and it was unclear what issues Rodgers was alluding to in the Steelers coach. Rodgers alleged that McCarthy is often behind on film, even days before a game. The quarterback also added that he isn’t the only Steeler with this point of view. “The entire team – offensively especially, really the entire team but offensively – they think that a change is needed because they see it,” Rodgers said. Rodgers said that during conversations with McCarthy, the head coach has denied the accusations. “At some point this stuff is going to get out and people are going to realize what is actually going on, it’s crazy and it shouldn’t be like that,” Rodgers said. The star quarterback added that he should be held accountable for vouching for the head coach before he was hired. “Full circle, with the first coach when I was starting, back in his hometown, there’s no way he’s going to sleep through his dream job,” he explained. The Pittsburgh Steelers host the Denver Broncos on Friday with Mason Rudolph stepping in at quarterback. This is a breaking story and will be updated.
